The only slightly negative comment is that the audio is a little tinny and not very loud. Alexa is much louder and have a wider range.

While this little speaker packs a punch volume-wise .. it just lacks the bass that other more expensive speakers have.
I do like that it stays ON with my echo dot and aux cable.
But music sounds a little too tinny, distorts on higher volume and not enough bass.
Still for the price .. it's a decent speaker

In the end I went with a JBL FLIP 3 .. and I am a lot happier now :)

I have Echo devices of one kind or another in every room and have had others that I’ve decided to let go (original Echo and Echo Auto). They’ve all performed their smarthome duties acceptably well. My biggest complaint across the board is sound quality. Alexa always sounds like she’s talking to you from underneath a pile of pillows. Bass? Sure, on the Echo Show, at least. Treble? Nada. Sure, you can use the app’s “equalizer”... but it’d take an oscilloscope to detect the minuscule difference that makes in the sound quality. I’d given up on getting any more devices... until I saw a review of the Flex on Paul Hibbert’s YouTube channel... he liked it, but said (I think) that it sounded ‘trebly’. Trebly?! That’s a magic word to my ears. I ordered one up and found that it indeed sounds ‘trebly’ (call it tinny of you like) but who cares? Who seriously listens to music on these tiny little devices anyway?! I can understand what Alexa says now - all the plosives are there. I still wonder why Amazon can’t tune the rest of the Alexa enabled devices for better higher frequency clarity.

I'm keeping this unit only because it fits the space that I wanted it in very well - I'm not at all happy with the performance of it.

I purchased this TV to mount on a very large desk that I have. The mounting is pretty straight-forward (they supply a cardboard drilling template and a few different spacer options). One thing to keep in mind on the mounting - make sure to allow for extra space for the speakers when drilling your mounting holes (the template does not have this space added).

Electronically, this is just a very average to below-average unit. I'm using cable as my video source. The TV that was in this location previously had an excellent picture. This unit has a snowy picture, and very poor color balance (I have tried adjusting it many times - it never does get a "good" picture).

The sound is awful. You have to create a balance between two different volume sources - one on the front of the main unit, the other on the TV itself (controlled by buttons on the TV, or by the remote). Between the two, if you turn it up to the point of what I would consider normal volume, you hear a faint but noticeable high-pitched whine (my Jack Russell Terrier hears it too...). The quality of the sound is pretty bad too - very thin and tinny. They should have added an Audio Out Jack, so that you could hook up a decent set of amplified speakers to it.

The Power button on the front of the unit is a cheap, spring-loaded design; I can tell that it will create problems in the long run (it has already stuck a few times).

The clock display is a bit annoying also - most digital displays will display the single-digit time without a zero in front nowadays - 3:00, for example. This clock displays it as 03:00.

The remote must use very unique frequencies - I was not able to program my regular Tivo remote to it (not even when cycling through the hundreds of preset codes that the Tivo remote has). I then purchased a "learning" Tivo remote - even that remote wouldn't accept the "power" or "volume down" functions ("volume up" was the only button that would accept the programming).

This speaker is OK. It's very portable, which is a plus, and I love the fact that it uses USB for power. The USB cable is a bit on the short side, but it's workable. The power/volume control and mute button are nice pluses. It's a bit on the tinny side, but what do you expect for such a small and inexpensive speaker? When desk real estate is tight, it gets the job done.

The Good: It's a computer monitor and works very well for that. Bright. Thin casing.
The Neutral: Controls are a bit hard to navigate and use, but after set-up, you would unlikely need to keep adjusting. This unit does use a brick transformer for power adding to the mess behind the desk. I would have like to just have a power cord directly into the monitor itself.
The Bad: As others said, the sound is horrible. low and tinny. If you want to watch rich media, this is not for you. If you just want sounds like mail notification, it's fine.

These are a well fitting good sounding and affordable set of on ear headphones. It's taken a while to get a comfortable fit but I've worn these comfortably for well over an hour. The sound is good. Nice bass response without being muddy and good treble reproduction without being tinny. One of my favorite features is the single wire design which makes for less tangle and easier wear. The cord is wrapped in either cloth or nylon (I'm not sure which) fabric. This set also comes with an inline microphone which I haven't really had any use for as of yet.

The Tivax 3.5-Inch Digital TV is also a multimedia device supporting multiple image, video and audio formats. Audio through the unit's single speaker is a bit tinny and slightly underpowered. At full or nearly full volume it's not all that loud. The unit does have a headphone jack and the addition of a set of decent buds or headphones will improve audio quality quite a bit although there are no bass or treble controls. It comes with a clear plastic screen protector and be warned, if you remove it getting it to lay perfectly flat again is nearly impossible.

Along with the headphone connector the TV also has a single Micro-SD memory card slot. I purchased a 2-GIG card to test this device with. I do not know, and the manual does not say, if the TV supports the newer, larger SDHC style cards. The device has NO user accessible internal memory.

All input and control are accomplished via two buttons on the face and a four way directional button set. The buttons are stiff and I found, with my thick fingers, that manipulating the directional arrow buttons was a bit hard to do with accuracy.

My unit, which is white as opposed to the stated black, arrived with a USB cable (which I have not used) an AC adapter/charger, an external antenna and a peg/tab stand on a lanyard. I found attaching the lanyard to the unit (you'll likely lose the stand otherwise) to be a complete pain and required a bent pin to accomplish.

Television Reception:
The Tivax 3.5-Inch Digital TV has a built in rod antenna which feels very fragile and easy to bend. The antenna also has a swivel base so care must be exercised when pushing it back into the unit. The included external antenna has a nicely long cord so it can be positioned easily for optimal reception. For the sake of reference I live approximately 80 miles South East of Orlando Florida on the coast. Using the built-in antenna, indoors, upon initial setup the channel scan was unable to find any stations. Plugging the external antenna in resulted in around a dozen channels being found during the setup scan. The 320x240 LCD screen images are crisp and sharp. Colors are vibrant and clear and I was pleasantly surprised at the adjustability of the picture including brightness, contrast, tint and color mode. Moving the television while watching TV should be avoided as the picture will often freeze and breakup. I was quite happy to find that one of the stations I do get is a 24/7 local area weather channel. During Florida's frequent power outages due to severe weather and hurricanes this will be invaluable.

Video Playback:
I loaded over a GIG of video files onto my Micro-SD card to test the Tivax's ability to playback video files. I chose a mixed batch of AVI, MPG, WMV and MOV file formats. WMV files are not supported at all (oddly the unit DOES support WMA audio files, go figure) and the support for the other formats was hit or miss. Approximately 60% of the fifty or so video clips I've tried to play were supported, but the rest just returned an error. Those that did play did so quite well. Picture quality was good (dependant, of course, on the quality of the videos) as was the audio playback. Perhaps they'll release a firmware update for the unit to add further CODEC support.

Audio Playback:
As I previously mentioned, the system's speaker is quite tinny. Don't expect great quality sound from it. It's not horrible but it could be better. I tested several dozen MP3 files on my Tivax including low (80 kbps) and very high (320 kbps) bit rate files as well as variable-bit rate encoded files and it played all of them without a problem.

Image Playback/Slide show:
The Tivax 3.5-Inch Digital TV supports JPEG, PNG, GIF and BMP image formats. Images display crisp and clean with bright and true colors. Landscape oriented images display best and while you can rotate images that are portrait oriented there is a distinct quality loss during rotation. Images can be zoomed in on with multiple levels of zoom.
The slide show feature is nicely configurable. The delay between images can be set or turned off for manual page turning. The transition effect done while changing images also has many options. The Tivax will also play any MP3 files in the same location as the images as background music during the slide show. I actually couldn't find a way NOT to have this happen if the audio and video files were mixed together on the memory card although the volume can be set to zero this will surely use more battery power even with the volume down.
One feature which I liked, but was not mentioned in the manual, is the ability to set one of your own images as the startup `logo'.

Power:
The Tivax 3.5-Inch Digital TV comes with a built in Lithium Ion battery which they state can be recharged approximately 500 times.
I found that their claimed charge durations were quite accurate. Watching Digital TV with the volume set to around 75% I was twice able to watch for a bit more than three hours before the unit turned off. I loaded several hundred large image files onto the memory card and set the unit to running them as a slide show (silent) and was able to achieve just over six hours of playback before the battery died. MP3 playback resulted in similar results of around five and a half hours of continuous play.
When charging there are NO indicator lights showing that the unit is charging nor any way, short of turning it on, to tell if it has fully charged. There is also no on screen low battery warning. When my battery was depleted the unit simply shut itself off.

Finally:
This is a nice unit and far more than just a digital TV set. A padded case would be a nice option. I'm going to try some of the smartphone cases to see if any fit. I really don't want to scratch or damage the screen. The external antenna while mildly magnetic really needs to be weighted and/or have a clip attached to it as it is rather light and hard to keep in place.

When I first took the radio from it's box, I thought I was the victim of a not-so-funny joke. This thing is tiny. How could it possibly do SW? How could it even have marginal sound? Well, it does just that and quite well, too.
I listen to 99.5 FM, the classical music station out of Boston. I'm over 60 miles away, yet day or night, the signal is as clear as a bell. The tiny speaker in this unit does an incredible job. It's not tinny or distorted. I can actually listen to Bach and not cringe.
This is my new pocket radio. It really is a quality product.

This a great radio in all three categories, be it AM, FM or SW. What's surprising is the speaker. Much better than those found on costlier radios. It doesn't have that tinny, give me a headache sound. Well made and more than worth the cost.

I sent it back. The sound on this unit drills into my skull 15 minutes after listening. Tinny and shrill. I've had $10 radios with smaller speakers that sound much, much better. Reception, however, is incredible. SW on this unit is great. Thus the two stars.
Tinny sound and on the lowest level it's too loud for a bedroom. I returned it.

These speakers have a tendency to be shrill and "bright" They do, however, reproduce sound of the CD fairly accurately and thus reveal the recordings' flaws .
They make longer listening tiresome.
They are not as good as the "real" Klipsch, the ones not made in China!
I can't tell if these are actually THX certified speakers ,as advertised. They did not do well with a THX DVD.
I finally gave up and sent them back. Too harsh. Ordered Audio Engine speakers.

I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because the sound quality of calls using the hands-free function is a little tinny, That is curious because when streaming music the sound quality if more than adequate.

What distinguishes this speaker - for me - are two things: (1) it's loud, and (2) the controls contain separate volume and skip buttons. Especially the latter because on speakers that combine those buttons I am forever skipping a track when I really wanted to increase or decrease volume. Not so on this speaker.

Some reviewers complained about hiss; I did not experience that at any volume level, even when the speaker was on, but not connected to my phone. Other complained about a loud announcement letting you know power on, pairing and the such. Yes, that is true. And you cannot change it or turn it off (that I know of). For me it is not a problem, but if stuff like that irritates you then you should be looking at different speakers instead of this one.

Sound quality is decent for a small speaker. The high frequency is stable and does not break up or get tinny at max volume. There may be a little compression, which most people like. I prefer truer reproduction. The mids are rich and I suspect that they are purposely biased to emphasize that frequency band. It definitely enhances casual listening, but if you are accustomed to true fidelity it may drive you nuts. The bass is not especially boomy. It's more than adequate if you listen to acoustic music and other genres, but for bass-centric music it's a little weak.

Volume is a surprise. This is a small speaker, but puts out a lot of sound. You can easily hear it from five to eight meters away when you have the volume cranked. Do be aware that you will more than cut play time in half if you max out the volume while on batteries. Still, you will get close to eight hours of play. The volume will cut through ambient noise, though, so this is ideal at the beach.

Bottom line: I view this as an entry-level speaker that is priced accordingly, but has some nice features compared to others in its range. Can you find a better speaker for the price? Possibly, although you will have to dig through a lot of product pages. Is this a safe choice? In my opinion, yes, as long as you can live with some of the issues that I mentioned.

I'll get the things I do not like about the review sample that I received out of the way first so I can finish on a positive note. Basically these phones have a distinct bias towards the higher frequencies, with a crossover to bass in my right ear and flat mid range response. In other words, if you are a critical listener you may want to consider other phones on the market.

I was able to get decent bass response in my right ear using my phone's EQ app, but could not get any decent mid range. The net result is music sounds one dimensional (even with the bass response in one ear.) I am guessing that the crossover threshold is such that you get high frequencies in one ear and low in the other, with the mid somehow cut out or deemphasized. For folks who listen to audio books and inspirational or educational material this will not be an issue. I will say that even with the volume cranked the high end did not break up or become tinny.

From a comfort perspective I had no problem wearing these for three hours with the medium buds that ship with it along with small and large ones. And I love the way they were securely held in place with the ear hooks.

Another feature that I like is the cable is flat and tangle-free. Of course, the nicest feature is they are, indeed, waterproof.

Bottom line: sound quality for music is lacking. However, if you are a casual listener and are into jogging, strenuous activities and wet environments these may be perfect. As much as I complained about the sound, I cannot find fault in the construction or ability to withstand harsh environments.

Being a lady approaching that certain age, my ears are not of the necessary construction to accommodate ear buds with any degree of comfort. Indeed, even the increasingly complicated act of bending at the waist can cause regular buds to become dislodged, so I approached these with some measure of reservation.

The memory foam did not feel much different to regular buds, but were not as reluctant to stay put as rubber buds. The construction is good, and the aesthetics are good, but still, they tend to hurt my ears after using them for a while.

I like the cloth covered cord, which feels a whole lot tougher than regular cords; and also the anti-tangle slider which works fine for me, but can be reduced in seconds to a tangled mess in the pocket of my ten year old son.

The big fat bass tends to overpower the higher frequencies a bit, but is still an improvement on other similarly priced models, especially as I prefer heavier bass over tinny trebly sound.

One minor improvement would have been if it had shipped with a case to store the extra buds which tend to get misplaced, and help with my son's tangling issues.

Amanda Richards, January 3, 2012

I would not, could not,
on a plane.
Not in the park. Not on a train.
Not in a car. Not on CD.
I do not like them, Sam, you see.
Not in my bed. Not on a boat.
Not on my head. Too big to tote.

When I first tried the earphones with the default ear tips, the sound was very "tinny". Highs, vocals, no discernible bass. Then when I was testing out the controls, I lightly pushed the earphones in my ear and wow - bass. I then replaced the ear tips with the larger ones in the set. Now they fit snug but comfortable. The sound is great. Bass is clear.

I use "Enter Sandman" by Metallica as one of my test songs. Cymbals = highs, vocals for mid, and great percussion for bass. The sound was fantastic, similar to my Sennheiser HD 280 pro.... Sennheiser is clearly better, but for small form factor earphones, Anker Soundcore Spirit X2 are a pleasure to use.

After almost 3 weeks with this television, I am amazed and very, very happy with it. There's a lot to like here and a couple of things that I wasn't expecting from any television.

First is the ease of set up. Our previous smart tv was a ROKU and reasonably simple to set up as well. The Google connection here means just signing in with your existing Google info and the tv uploads your existing apps. Just like moving to your new Android phone or tablet. All of our streaming apps populated and we were able to sign in without drama - HBOMAX, Prime, Paramount Plus, HULU and Netflix. We only stream and haven't used cable or satellite in 5 years, so easy app access with a new tv is important.

The 4K picture is outstanding. There's no distortion in picture quality or digital noise even from old 1940s movies. The colors are rich and full and the tv settings let you adjust to your preference as well. We've watched a lot, A LOT of tv recently and every show on all platforms has been gorgeous. Frankly, we probably watch way too much tv as a rule and that's not going to change. I've been amazed at the picture quality difference between our year old HD tv and this one.

We've connected Alexa to this tv and the voice controls work...most of the time. Using the voice control via the remote control renders better responses for sure. The tv has recognized a Fire stick, Roku Express stick, and a portable DVD player for us without any drama. We don't have a gaming system, though.... I'm considering buying one for this giant screen.

But my final show stopper moment with this television has been the sound quality. We've never had a tv that didn't require a sound bar. Until now. Despite the tv being quite thin and lightweight, the speakers still produce a deep sound quality without any tinny undertones. The settings have a calibration option for the speakers that you definitely need to do for the best sound - it works. I truly believe this is the best television we've ever owned.

I keep a sensor at the point where the driveway opens to the barn area so I know if someone is arriving while I am doing horse stuff. Our old one lasted several years, so I hope this one lives up to that standard.

This one just went on the same fence post hook as the old one. The sensor is about 38 feet away just inside the barn door overhang - so it's a very short distance. (I can't speak the 500 foot claims)This system allows you to choose from several different alert sounds and that's nice... Our old one had a single shrill shriek that got old fast. So far this is working correctly and doing the job without problems.

We've never had a projector before and this is a reasonable beginner/introductory projector. It helped us realize that we're not really projector people for a couple of reasons. It works best in a completely dark room or outside with no residual daylight or street lights. We found the best picture came from using the the included screen out on the patio around 9pm. The picture wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't really 1080p using the Roku stick. Going outside in the summer here for a movie is a cute idea, but this is Texas and it's just too humid and miserable for that.

The projector has speakers built in, but they are small and the sound is tinny. You can connect a sound bar if yours uses the RCA type cables - niether of my bars do. They only use HDMI or Digital optical line and the projector only has one HDMI port and no optical audio line. So we're just stuck with the built in speakers. I'm not unhappy with this unit, but I don't see us using it often at all.

I have had my main Echo since the first days after the initial invitation to buy was sent out. I absolutely love Alexa and use her for tons of things daily. - she lives in the hallway between the living room and kitchen where we spend the most time. I added the Dot a month ago to bring the Alexa functions into our master bedroom.

The Dot is as easy to use as the big Echo and now that the two can be connected, we have music throughout the house at the same time. I also like the intercom skill so we can talk to each other across the house quickly. My one dislike is the tinny sounding small speaker n the Dot. I've grown so accustomed to the balanced, clean sound from the big Echo that the Dot sound quality was a let down with music. However, reading me the news, ordering Starbucks, reading my audio books, working as an alarm clock or intercom is smooth and works just fine. I especially like being able to control our tv with Alexa voice commands - we cut the cable cord and stream via Prime, Netflix and Hulu Live and Alexa has made searching for a specific show much more simple.

I bought this television new from wally world on one day sale for under three hundred bucks and it has turned into an excellent purchase that I would have been happy with had I paid full price for it. We have the 50" unit and it was extremely easy to unpack, attach the included swivel stand, and place it on our entertainment center by myself. The entire tv weighs around 20lbs maybe - it's light enough for me to pick it up without strain. There are three HDMI outlets, a single USB outlet, the usual RCA plug-ins, the cable connection, and a digital audio connection for use with a sound bar.

The picture is clear and sharp and easy to adjust for our personal tastes with regard to color temperature, contrast, and brightest etc. There is no stuttering or shadowing watching sports or other fast moving live action. We have it connected to our cable box and a DVD player through the HDMI cables and the Amazon Fire Stick on the USB - all work correctly and are easy to swap between.

My one complaint is the native speakers are tinny and thin sounding, but that seems to simply be a fact of life with large flat screen televisions. I bought the Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding to enhance the sound. The digital audio connection was a snap to connect and the box comes on as soon as the tv powers on. The two pieces operate as one and our living room has become the center of our evenings again....movies are a pleasure to watch and listen to. 45 days with this Sceptre tv and I am very pleased so far - it's every bit as good as our smaller Samsung for far less money.

I was very surprised at how powerful this little pod speaker actually is - it really does have a significant amount of volume and can be used in your car if you don't have a blue-tooth enabled system (for example my Mother's 10 year old Suburban out at the ranch) or at the barn when working horses in the round pen or dressage arena. It works via a standard blue-tooth connection or using the NFC option if your smart phone is equipped. There is also a microphone built in and the speaker does in fact, work very well with phone calls - we placed and received two calls using this as a speaker phone and the calls were a tad "tinny", but if you need to speak to someone hands free while cooking a meal or grooming a horse and you don't want a traditional headset, this is an excellent option.

I tested this speaker both inside and outside and it kept the signal from my Amazon Fire Phone almost 60 foot away outside in a direct line of sight with no degradation playing music. Inside the house, it managed to retain a strong signal through a closed door for about 30 feet before it lost the connection and that was far better performance than a no name blue tooth speaker we bought at Hastings in December. Sound quality is pretty good with both classical and country music. Pop can be a bit hollow at upper volume levels and hard rock has reasonable bass sound, but the vocals tend to become somewhat shrill to my ears. This is not a big deal in the least - just turn down the volume and know that at this price range you're buying the idea of portability rather than some super hi tech music snob gizmo.

Connecting this TechMatte Sound Pod to my Amazon Fire phone was super easy & took literally 10 seconds via NFC. It also connected just as easily to a Samsung Galaxy S2 and a Samsung Galaxy Note 1st Generation. My one complaint is that the on/off switch is directly over the charging outlet, so you have to disconnect the charging cable to turn it on or off and then reconnect the cord if you need it to charge or want to power it via the outlet while in use. A minor irritant that is at most worth a half star deduction. Overall, this is a very nice portable speaker that does exactly what it claims to do and fits in the palm of your hand. I did receive a sample speaker to test and review.

OK, let's get this straight at the beginning: I'm not an audio expert. I don't work in the industry, I haven't studied this stuff, etc. But I DO know what sounds good especially when it comes to classical music recordings. I've been involved in classical music my whole life, I've played and sung with orchestras, so I know how things should sound.

Bottom line: this unit produces very good quality sound over the range of dynamics and timbres that come with a variety of classical music. I have a few recordings that I use as "tests": Carmina Burana (the opening "O Fortuna" section); Bach "Magnificat"; Stravinsky "Firebird"; Mozart piano sonatas; Beethoven String Quartets; and various choral works (Eric Whitacre, Brahms, etc.). I got none of the tinny sound that sometimes happens with piano works; the softer sections of the Eric Whitacre choral works were clear and precise; the range of dynamics in the opening O Fortuna of "Carmina Burana" was crystal clear with no distortion. Really, this outperformed my expectations.

The unit is smaller than I expected, which is a good thing, since I intend to take it along when I travel. It's attractive (I got the orange color), and has a nice "feel" to it. The controls are easy to manipulate on the top of the unit, and I really like the ability to take phone calls via the unit (it has a built-in microphone).

Overall, I'm very pleased with this purchase. I paid less than forty dollars for mine, and at that price, I consider it a super deal. I've had it only for a couple of weeks, so if there are issues with durability, I'll update this review. For now, it's definitely worth 5 stars.

When see you're buying Bose and the $200 price, you automatically think you're going to get a crystal clear, high quality sound from this soundbar. But you don't get that.

What I got was sound that was not all that noticeably better than the speakers built into my new-model big-screen Vizio TV. Yes, I am connecting the TV to the Bose Soundbar using the optical cable. So disappointing.

What sets the INNOCN 15.6" portable monitor apart from other type-c portable monitors is the built in battery and the touch screen features. In the box, a soft silicone case is included with a cover that folds into a stand, making it feel like an oversized tablet.

Other portable monitors with built-in battery are usually a little bit thicker or have a bulge at back of the screen. The INNOCN doesn't have that. It is a thin slab that is around 3/8" thick. I actually use it as a secondary screen on a daily basis and while the monitor has an all aluminum casing, there is almost no heat generated by the screen during use.

The touch capability of this monitor brings touch support to any Windows PC without the need for drivers but even more, connect this to an Android phone such as my LG V40 and not only does the phone go into desktop mode, the touch screen works to turn the phone into a 15.6" tablet! The built-in battery will help to keep the phone topped off and allow fully wireless (no need to plug into the wall, but there will be a wire between phone and screen) tablet.

My previous monitor was a LePow 15.6" type-c portable Monitor. It is representative of many other portable monitors on the market. Compared to the INNOCN, the INNOCN is a lot brighter and the colors more vibrant. The LePow was instant on but the INNOCN can take about 2-3 seconds to turn on after receiving a signal. Both have speakers that are tinny and quite weak, but serviceable if you're on-the-go.

If you are purchasing this monitor to work with the Nintendo Switch, you will be disappointed. The Switch is very picky about the conditions that must be met before it goes into docked mode, mainly a 19v type-c PD. The power output from this monitor simply doesn't supply that, even when plugged in to an original Nintendo power adapter (the adapter will serve to charge the screen, but will not supply the 19v to the connected switch). It will only work with the switch through a dock, which really defeats the purpose of a portable monitor. On the other hand, the LePow does actually does work with the switch. Connected a power adapter or portable phone charger to the LePow and the monitor will supply the necessary 19v to the Switch.

So overall, a great monitor for most uses, especially the ability to turn a phone into a large touchscreen tablet, but if you want a portable large-screen solution for the Nintendo Switch, go for something like the LePow

As an old, retired guy, I find technology still significantly impacting my daily life in two ways. The first is that I spend a lot of time every day online - either gaming in my favorite MMO or binge watching the various streaming services. The second way is that I keep in touch with my far-flung network of family and friends via social media. Now, my desktop pc handles the first of those two very nicely. The problem is that I can get immersed for hours in gaming or in a good streaming show. Social media notifications break that immersion, causing me to move away from whatever I was doing to see what the latest notice was about. If I don't, it could be quite a while before I get around to checking my social media and responding to the messages there.

This is where a tablet comes in. I figured it would be nice to have a tablet that quietly beeped new notifications and allowed me to just glance over at the latest notice to see if it needed a quick response or not. Little did I know how hard it would be to find a low end tablet capable of that simple task. This is the fourth tablet I've tried and the first one which could do that one simple thing for me. The other low end tablets quickly crashed and burned for a variety of reasons. This is the first that actually continued to work after the first few days, giving me the notifications I wanted and that I could check out at a glance.

There are some issues with this tablet that folks should be aware of. The sound is tinny enough that I wouldn't listen to music or audiobooks on this thing. The visual quality is sufficient for modern movies and tv shows but vintage ones do look a bit fuzzy. The charge doesn't last quite as long as I'd like it to. The tablet needs to be charged twice a day, even when it's just sitting there beeping when a text message or email comes in. Charging once a day would be nicer but it is what it is. Still, this is the first low end tablet of four I've tried that actually does the simple task I want it to do. So for that, I have to give it a solid 4 star rating.

As an old, retired guy, tech factors into my daily life in two important ways. The first way is that I spend hours every day online, playing my favorite MMO. The second is that my extended family, spread across the United States, stays in touch via social media. The very specific niche I got this tablet to fill was for a way to get social media notifications that wouldn't disrupt my gaming. I first tried an Amazon 7" Fire Tablet. The audio notification on that tablet died after the first day or two. There was also no way I could find to turn off the sleep function. The tablet kept shutting down so I couldn't just look over to visually see if there any notifications.

This Android tablet works perfectly to fill that niche. It sits quietly next to my main computer screen and gives a soft audio notification when I get an email or a text message. A glance shows me the first lines of the text or email, letting me know if a quick response is needed or not. The notifications were easy to set up and the sleep function is set to Never. So this tablet does exactly what I want it too.

There are some issues with it that you should be aware of though. For one thing, it charges slowly but drains quickly. For another, turning it back on sometimes takes a bit of extra button pushing. It looks like it is coming on but then shuts off again. At times I've had to hit the power button 4-5 times before it turns all the way on. Videos are just on the edge of being grainy while the audio is distinctly tinny, without any depth. I sometimes listen to audiobooks while gaming but the sound is just too tinny and irritating to listen to them on this tablet.

Since this product does exactly what I want it to, I have to give it a 4 star rating. Other than my specific niche use though, this is a basic, entry level product, which is why I can't give it 5 stars. It just doesn't have the high end quality of far more expensive tablets.

The tablet came charged, which was nice, but the problems started very quickly after first turning it on. After connecting my email and turning on a YouTube video, the tablet kicked me off in a few minutes. It then glitched when trying to turn it back on, taking something like 45 tries before it actually started working again. I'm watching another video right now and the image is grainy while the audio is tinny. Photos taken with the built in camera are also very grainy and poor quality. If you need a cheap tablet and have low expectations for it, this might work. If you need a quality product though, pass on this one.

EDIT: After a few days of usage, this tablet finally crashed and won't turn back on again. It is now worthless and I am dropping my rating to 1 star to reflect that sad reality.

Somewhere there is an ancient marketing survey that identifies teen-age boys as a prime segment of the gaming market and that says they really like bright, flashing lights. So manufacturers who want to sell to the gaming market still think they have to add flashy lighting to all their products. Well, the gaming universe is much larger than teen boys these days and bright, flashing lights have nothing to do with playing a game. With that pet peeve off my chest let me add a couple of things to give this review some context. First, I do spend a lot of time online playing an MMO but I'm very much a casual player, not a hardcore competitive one. Second, I am not an audiophile. High end stereo gear is wasted on me as the music coming from most any clock radio is good enough for me.

To my non-audiophile ears, the sound from this speaker is fine. It provides a nice range without being too heavy on the bass end or too shrill on the high end. Whether gaming, streaming videos, or listening to music and audiobooks, this speaker holds its own nicely. Though, like the flashy lighting, the sound quality really doesn't make any significant difference while I'm playing in my MMO world. The ambient noise, NPC chatter, battle music and such, all come through nicely but that's a perk, not something that particularly improves my game play.

The under the monitor design of this speaker really doesn't save me any desk space. The mini speakers I was using before were much smaller and were out of the way on the side of the monitor. This space bar basically sits in front of my monitor and takes up more room than other speakers. One strong plus to me for this speaker is the fact that it really is plug and play. I had it up and running in just a few minutes. Other "gaming" gear I've tried with flashy lighting systems require software to control the lighting and sometimes getting that software to install and run properly can be a major, frustrating effort. So I really, really like that this product lives up to its "plug and play" claim.

There is one last negative point to mention. a minor one. The volume and other controls are flat buttons on the side of the soundbar. So to adjust the volume, change the lighting, etc, you need to move the soundbar to look at the side of it so you can see what you are doing. I call that a minor issue because my keyboard has mute and volume control buttons on it and I can just use those to adjust the sound as needed.

The bottom line of all this for me is that I wouldn't buy this speaker as a "gaming speaker" but simply as a nice mid-range speaker who's sound quality I like, one that is easy to set up and use. Oh, and lest I sound too much like a Grinch, the lights really are pretty, the way Christmas lights are. It's just that they have nothing to do with gaming. :)

I am always on the lookout for radios to use in an emergency. Having lived through an extended outage during severe weather emergency for several weeks, not having any way to find out what was going on was difficult.

SIZE
This radio is a nice small size. Picture two juice boxes standing next to each other side by side. It fits just about anywhere. If you want to take it on a trip or camping, it has a very small footprint for packing.

CHARGING
Charging this is either micro USB, crank, or solar. I would say solar is more of a way to keep the radio trickle charged. I would not use that as my primary source as it takes a long time.

SOUND
The sound is really really nice. I am shocked at how nice this little unit sounds. It has great bass and midtones without sounding tinny or far away.

FLASHLIGHT
In an emergency having this as a flashlight is handy, although I would not use it unless no other options were there.

CHARGING PHONES?
I have not used it for charging phones. I keep power banks for that.

ALARM CLOCK/CLOCK
This is a great feature if you are camping or if you have to be up at a certain time during a power outage due to expected weather, checking on sump pumps, etc. It works well if you follow the instructions.

SD CARD
This plays music from an SD card and I have to say the sound is great.

CHARGING TIME
This took a few hours to charge up for us. Between 3 and 4.

PERFORMANCE
When running the radio, we got several days. We did not have it full volume, and we only played it a few hours at a time, not continually.

LOW BATTERY LIGHT
This has a low battery light which is a great feature. It helps you not let it run dry in power.

RECEPTION
The reception is excellent for FM, Very good for AM (some stations don't come in as well), and WB is also hit and miss, but still way nicer than most radios of this type that I have had.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a fantastic little radio. The sound is way nicer than expected and performance is great. Lots of great features make this handy to have.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is one of my favorite radios so far. It is really nice to work with and all of the power sources work well.

Our family is a bunch of speaker and ear phone fanatics. Everyone has different likes and I tend to like a well balanced music. Muffled really bugs me.

I wanted to have a nice balanced speaker that no one will take so I decided to get this one for ME. It has a nice solid housing and I figured it was worth getting since my favorite speaker seems to get misplaced a lot. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a very solid speaker. It is heavy duty and it has metal housing. The sides are not as fragile as others I have used which sound this good. It comes in a beautiful gift box which has cushioning and the typical Santana design to it. The speaker itself is pretty heavy so it is not something you toss in your backpack and run off with. It needs a bit more care than that.

CHARGING
This has a USB charger that will take about 4 hours to charge it up with. There is also a connection where you can get a FAST charger from the company, but you have to contact them for it. The charging cable comes with it just need a USB outlet. The directions warn to only use the original cable that comes with this to charge or there might be damage to the speaker. The voltage must be 5V with current rated at 115A.

CAN THIS RUN WHILE CHARGING?
I do not see in the instructions warnings against this, and it does work while plugged in.

PLAY TIME
This speaker runs out of juice pretty quickly. If you want it to last the entire time of 10 hours, I highly suggest you not put the volume up past 30%. Any higher and the battery time runs down pretty quickly. At 60% you are at the edge of running this down pretty quickly- as in 4 or 5 hours play time only.

PAIRING
I have had no issues pairing this with tablets or phones using Android. Just like when you turn the power on, it says PAIRING in a very loud voice so you will know when it is in pairing mode.

VOLUME
The volume button on this is tricky. If you are not thinking and just quickly press the volume once, instead of it getting slightly louder, you will skip a track. You have to press the volume down and not let up if you want the sound to go up or down depending on the button you press meaning +/-.

CARD SLOT
This speaker can also work off of a TF card (also known as a microSD card). You just have to change from bluetooth mode to card mode using the MODE button.

IS THERE AUX CAPABILITY?
I have an old MP3 player that has higher quality recordings than anything new I have. That only uses AUX and it works great with this.

PAUSE / PLAY
You can pause or play music with this using the MFB button

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
Let me tell you, this thing ROCKS. I mean it. This speaker is fabulous. Not only does it work great out of the box (after being fully charged) but it sounds better and better as you break it in. It fills the house with music that is great quality and does not have interference or any lag issues either.

WHAT ABOUT BASS, MIDS AND HIGHS?
I have to say that this speaker is one of the few that I have used which does a beautiful job of intense bass, balanced clear highs but the mids are not muffled at all. It is impressive and what I thought a speaker always should be.

CAN YOU USE TWO TOGETHER?
This allows you to add one other speaker to the system so you can have them in two places. I do not have another Europa speaker at the moment I can test that with.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although this blows any other wireless speaker I have had out of the water, it does blow through power rather quickly unless the volume is pretty low. It is not only amazing out of the box (After charging) but it gets better with more use. This baby ROCKS.

MY RATING
Finding a speaker which does not overwhelm you with out of whack bass, piercing highs, or muffled middles is not always easy. This speaker seems to divide it all out very well. It is one of the nicest speakers I have used (wireless) to date. FIVE STARS!

Not only do I love this, but would definitely consider a second one along with the fast charger in the future to round out the whole system.

ANOTHER THING
This product has a notification on it that some of the proceeds from this product will go to help underprivileged children through the MILAGRO foundation (miracle) that Carlos Santana and his family started in 1998.

(WARNING- This is an in depth review of this laptop. My goal is to help those who are truly interested in making informed buying decisions. This is done from an experiential point of view of most consumers and not highly technical. If you prefer a shorter summary, see paragraph titled, THE BOTTOM LINE)

WHAT IS THIS LAPTOP LIKE?
I have had a lot of different tablets, laptops, desktops, and have built my own systems over the years. One thing I have not had is a hybrid laptop which changes from tablet to laptop and back again. I was not too fond of a 15 inch size as I tend to like smaller laptops, but I was willing to try. I am SO glad I did.

COVERING/CASE OF LAPTOP
This laptop is a thin profile, but feels very substantial. The bottom does not have tiny little rubber feet like some HP professional laptops I have had, but it has solid large rubberized pads that are 1 inch by a half inch. There are a decent amount of vents in the bottom as well. The top is a slightly textured metallic top (etched look) and not shiny. The hinges are very strong and hold the screen in a variety of directions solidly. They do not budge until I move them again.

SIZE
I am amazed that this is the first 15 inch laptop that I actually enjoy using! The size and way that it works makes it fantastic for me. I can tilt the screen in any direction and use my hands on the screen or keyboard in laptop mode which is a pleasure.

KEYBOARD
The keyboard is soft touch and rubberized key-wise. As soon as I touch the keys, a back light comes up so that I can see what I am doing. The back light goes out in 15 seconds or so when the keys are not being pressed. There is a full numerical keyboard and plenty of room between keys for my medium sized fingertips. It is also spaced well for those who have longer nails.

SCREEN
The screen is shiny. It doubles as a screen as well as touchscreen. The view on the screen is fabulous as it has a full HD 1080 resolution. The colors are not as intense as the Saumsung Galaxy Tab S2, which is one of the most amazing color screens I have worked with. Since I am a person who likes color, I like color intensity in my screens. However, this screen is fine and is by no means pale, it is just not quite as intense as I am used to.

TOUCHSCREEN
When you flip the keyboard back, the touchscreen clicks into place. You are given the option to choose the touchscreen if you want so there are no mistakes. As a tablet, I have found that it is very accurate and works quite well. I have put it through a lot and so far, I have only had a few instances where I was frustrated for a second, but it was easy to correct.

OPERATION
This turns on so fast it is almost jolting. My laptops, though usually professional level, often take quite a bit to boot up. This one, however is so quick it always surprises everyone here.

As for operations, I have found this to be a very fast and easy to use system. Load up is quick and the only problems I have from time to time are due to wireless and not really the fault of the laptop.

Turning it off sometimes makes me laugh out loud. Press button. BAM! It’s off.

WINDOWS 10
I am not a fan of Windows 10. But unfortunately that is pretty much the choice for any laptop at this point. This laptop seems to handle it very well.

GAMES
Because Windows 10 is not as game friendly as previous operating systems, I have not had the time to mess around with games with this. I have avoided Windows 10 until now, so I have not figured out what if any games will work with this. I will update when I do.

RUN TIME
Charging seems to take only a few hours for a full charge. The run time varies between 3 and 5 hours depending on what I am doing. I will say this- I rarely run it into the ground in one sitting, which makes it very helpful for me.

VIDEO
Runs very smooth on here. Using a DVD player means I have to use the USB port to run my independent unit and be in a stable position to do so. Works well. Beautiful to watch.

USB PORTS AND SD READER
I have found the USB ports to work very well. No problems to this point. Load up is fast. Using the SD reader is also a pleasure. The photos load up fast and due to the high resolution screen viewing them is really detailed and helpful. I have not installed professional graphics software yet to test this system for photo editing.

TOUCH PAD (AND FRUSTRATION)
The touch pad on this laptop is a bit challenging to use. There is a finger reader which I do not use, but the buttons are hidden in the pad itself and not two different buttons. The pad is pretty accurate as far as tracking. The only problem I have is location. When I rest my left hand on the rest area, sometimes it interferes with the touch pad and causes things to go a bit crazy at times. I am not pressing ON the touch pad, just in the area next to it.

SOUND
The sound is not tinny or awful. I find that it is sufficient for most of the applications I want to use it for. If I prefer to have a better sound, I use my Soundbot speaker and that gives me even better sound for movies and videos.

COMMENTS
I have to say that although the touch pad situation does frustrate me now and then, I do love this laptop. I have always wanted a hybrid because since I started using tablets, I would always catch myself touching the screen when I was using one of the household laptops and it was frustrating.

This unit is really nice. It is so fast and easy to use, it surprises me, honestly. It is so easy to switch between tablet and laptop modes and I find it a pleasure to work with for photos and movies.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This hybrid is VERY fast, easy to use, and boots up and shuts down so fast it is startling. The screen is a pleasure to look at, although not as color saturated as Samsung can be. So far, USB and SD works great. Sound is good enough for most applications. This is easy to use and not at all cumbersome. I love that I can touch the screen even in laptop mode if I am frustrated with the touch pad. I am very happy with this laptop/tablet hybrid.

RATING
FIVE STARS! I will update if I have anything else to add in the future, but at this point, I am very happy with this.

For moderate priced earbuds, these are pretty good. The sound quality is much better than average, with smooth response across the range. The highs are detailed, and not shrill. The midbass is clear, with no unnatural peak that sometimes passes for "bass boost". The deep bass is natural, and not artificially strong. Very easy to listen to for extended sessions.

For comfort, these are pretty average -- not the best comfort, but not bad either. There are interchangeable ear tips you can try out for the best fit. There's a lot of personal preference as to what's going to stay in the ear comfortably. The earbuds are angled, so you have to pay attention to the left/right orientation.

This is advertised as "iPhone compatible", meaning that there's a mic with tiny + and - buttons attached to the left ear piece. I'm a BlackBerry guy, and I'm happy to report that the mic works fine with my BlackBerry Bold 9700. But the + and - buttons don't have any effect (they don't raise or lower the volume). However, pressing the small button between the + and - buttons will either pause the song that's playing, or mute a phone call. Pretty handy.

Sound isolation is not a strong point of this set. I wasn't sure what to expect, so I guess I'm not disappointed. Probably you'd want to look elsewhere if sound isolation is important to you.

Durability may also be an issue. The wire is very thin, and it feels fragile, especially where it connects to the earbud. I'll know in 6 to 12 months whether these will stand up to regular use. The 90-degree plug will take wear better for many people, depending on how it connects to your phone, MP3 player or computer. Comes with a little storage pouch, which is good protection for the set when not in use.

(Yes, all three together.) The volume was weak, even when turned up to max. Then as I was looking for more music to try, I heard an ugly scratchy hiss, and thought my laptop's fan was acting up. Nope, it was the speakers. Yes, they produce a nasty noise when idle, and it doesn't go away, stays there so you can hear it under the music if you listen carefully.

To me that makes these speakers fail the basic test. Especially when you consider that you can get better speakers for about half the money, and a whole lot better for similar money, these are just unacceptable. Therefore the 1star rating.

(In case you would like a recommendation: I have a pair of Altec Lansing speakers that I think are really very good for desktop computer speakers, with rich clear well-balanced sound.)

It does the job, and I have a fairly powerful and functional computer, but on consideration I think I should have considered some of the alternatives instead.

The most frustrating problem has been unaccounted for behavior with Windows 7, apparently related to the mobo. For instance, wake from sleep consistently crashes the computer (I checked the dumps to verify that it was definitely a wake-related crash), and there is (as yet) no bios or driver update to fix it. Ok, sleep isn't that important, I can live without it. But sometimes a simple reboot will hang, apparently in the same place, right when Windows should be booting up. A forced shutdown (holding the power button for several seconds) and restart fixes that problem. But neither of these is really expected, or acceptable.

A lesser problem is the sound -- somehow it's tinny, sounds worse than the audio on my 5-year old mid-range computer. I'm probably going to buy an audio card, which shouldn't have been necessary.

The onboard networking is just fine, I haven't had any problems with it. The onboard video is ok as well, but I didn't test that too much since I added a separate video card.

I think I should have gone with MSI or Asus instead, and that's what I'm going to look at when my son & I build a mid-price gaming rig for him later this fall.

I find the skill set/setup dubious and the Alexa app was slow and very glitchy. This review is strictly about the device as a streaming Wi/Fi/Bluetooth speaker and sound quality.

I am an Amazon Prime customer and all my music is on Amazon streaming. Both ease of use (on Amazon Music/Pandora, etc. only) and sound in one word, Superb! I'm completely surprised because I own the $200+ UEBoom (which has been sitting unused on a shelf, I had to go look for it) and assumed the sound on that would be much superior as reviews and it's reputation suggest. Not so! I just listened back to back.

Without intending to compare them, I got my UEBoom to play while I setup the marvelous SOAIY Aurora projector (upgraded version), and in the back of my mind notice the music, not played very loudly because it's nighttime, was rather muddy; I think it wows people for its volume and base. On a whim I switched to my new Amazon Tap received today (I hadn't much time to experiment with it) and... Wow! Fantastic sound quality! Much more enjoyable than the popular UEBoom.

Better flat frequency response like a pair of reference headphones (like the Sony Studio MV6 I prefer), more clear definition and detail, not muddy, better treble response (I don't mean tinny or lack of bass), and bass rivaling that of UEBoom. Oh, the main thing I noticed also, which confused me at first, is the wide stereo dispersion (?), um, I mean wide field effect and stereo separation. I literally looked at the cylinder puzzled as to what I was hearing and mentally verifying only this device was on and was the source of the sound I was hearing.

The UEBoom always sounded merely monaural from one sourcepoint; this sounded like surround sound effect applied to a two-speaker (not 5.1+) tv. I was amazed at what my senses were reporting to me. Okay, I'm going to say it, to my ears, and I have a class D amplifier and 5 pairs of quality headphones of different brands, the sound of this Amazon Tap is superior, right out of the box. I was amazed. And of course streaming directly sans device is certainly more convenient. It "just works". (After connecting to your Wi-Fi network.)

I learned to say "playlist rock", since I have a playlist named rock, or it will play all my Amazon music in the genre "rock". I did ask for the weather after entering my zip code through the Alexa app, which I dislike, and it responded with detailed information. Luckily music playback works directly without a need for app use. I will now mention this superior sound quality is half the price of it's aforementioned similar-sized competitor. I'm now really glad I bought it :)

Both the image and audio quality from this camera have always been disappointing. I didn't really know just how poor it was until I owned an iPhone 4S, which captures vastly superior video, and mono audio that sounds much better than the tinny stereo captured by the Picsio.

And then there's the problem with mysteriously aborted video recordings, which has happened twice to me. The first time I missed part of a dance performance, but that was mostly an annoyance at the time, since it was an ad-hoc recording and I simply switched to my phone. The second time, I missed a good chunk of a recital I'd been asked to video for a friend. The recording stopped unexpectedly and retained only 1 second of the segment. I had started the recording, watched a few seconds to confirm that it going, and sat down. 9 minutes later someone notified me that the display had gone black and it hadn't been blinking for the previous two songs. When I hit the power button and it woke up (!?!?), the display said something about "file" and "management" and "update", and after trying to get it to come on and start recording, it said "update complete" or "finished" and then it recorded the remainder of the performance. (Pardon me if I don't remember the exact on-screen messages.) I had an hour of capacity (in iFrame mode) left on the card, which was freshly formatted, and the camera was on DC power so that batteries wouldn't be an issue. There was no discernible reason for this to have happened.

Bottom line: I can't trust this camera, and I won't even try to resell it or give it to someone; I wouldn't want to do that to someone else. For more serious video, I dropped the coin on a Canon VIXIA (which is fantastic), and for casual video, I'll use my iPhone. Either way, I will never rely on this camera again.

Now, for my one complaint. The button for pausing is so so tiny and it doesn't have a lot of clickiness so its a little hard to know if you have engaged pause or not so I end up pushing pause twice and then it unpauses. But, I'll get used to it eventually.

If all you watch is driven by an external device like a cable box or Roku or something, then this is probably an acceptable TV for you. However, you're paying a good chunk of money to have a "smart" TV that can connect to services like Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Hulu, and that "smart" technology is terrible.

- The video streaming apps crash regularly, or go unresponsive, or will have significant delays, or even lock up so badly that you have to reboot the TV. And since there's no volume-equalizing feature, sometimes a quiet TV show will crash and abruptly you'll be sent back to the default "TV Plus" music channels, blaring a country song at ear-splitting volumes.

- Those same apps sometimes receive forced updates without any notice. One day you'll turn on the TV and discover that the controls are different or even missing. For example, my son loves the "Classical Baby" series via Amazon, and would frequently used the "restart season from the beginning" button to watch it again. Then one day, poof, no more button. To watch it again, we have to navigate back to the first episode, resume it (which picks up about 4 seconds from the end), and quickly start rewinding all the way back to the beginning of the episode. This itself is not a huge deal but the same type of unexpected, forced-on-you changes have happened many times in the last 2 years of owning the TV.

- The "dynamic" picture mode looks good on a few shows but on others will seriously distort colors. Skin will be bluish, or someone's red coat will be super-saturated into a weird blob of red on the screen. It also increases the refresh rate so things suddenly lose the normal movie feel and instead get that soap opera feel to them.

- It doesn't support the normal phone "cast" features that pretty much every other TV and phone supports. It supposedly supports a screen mirroring feature via their own SmartThings mobile app but the configuration is so awful and inconsistent that I have yet to get any casting to work (I'm a techie so these things are not often difficult). Why wouldn't they just go with the normal way that everyone else does it, which works flawlessly? Who knows.

Maybe in the future, Samsung will get their act together but right now it's a very bad buy for most people.

The first thing I noted when I listened to these much-celebrated headphones (at least the Prestige line at any rate) is how incredibly exaggerated the low-end is. While getting that kind of bass response from a headphone driver is impressive, showing it off at the expense of fidelity is not something I particularly care for. When using these on a device where a DAC is involved, such as an iPad, I have to use the 'bass reducer' EQ profile on the device or the sound will otherwise will be muddy with distortion. I am sure this has a lot to do with the dinky amplifier inside the iPad being unable to fully drive the the whopping 32 ohms of resistance the SR80e pushes back with. As a rule, underpowered amplifiers are what ruin the drivers inside speakers or headphones so when you hear distortion it means your amplifier is underpowered when matched with the driver and you need to change one of those two things. When you hear distortion from a crappy amplifier that's the sound of your speakers being slowly ruined so you really want to avoid this. (I always have a sad chuckle when some punk is walking the streets with ghetto blaster at maximum volume and the sound is atrocious- little does he know that what people are annoyed by is not the volume, but the distortion! Plus he's ruining his equipment.)

Using the SR80e with a mobile device is a case where an external headphone amplifier would be highly desirable, if not required, so this is a bit of an ask. I have not had a lot of success with the in-line amplifiers designed to run off of the device's power (specifically the Lightning-DAC-and-amplifier combos that you can buy to replace the dongle that Apple ships with their new iPhones) where I played recordings which have very high amplitude levels. For these recordings, the distortion is intolerable even though records at a nominal recording level sound great. The lack of gain control is a real problem with these gadgets- something that is de-facto on any headphone amp that you don't put in your pocket. Therefore, you'll be reduced to using headphones like these at home or work, which is where I use mine.

The fact that you have to significantly alter the EQ profile of your audio player to even have these cans reproduce a sound that is remotely like the original recording violates "high fidelity" by definition. Compare this to a sound engineer style headphone set like Sony MDR Pros which are designed to reproduce the source signal as accurately as possible. This is what "high fidelity" actually means. Some people may not like this and will end up using some artificial bass boost on their device to compensate, which the MDRs will gladly deliver. Most people who listen to popular music are generally accustomed to excessive bass. If that is the sort of listener that you are, then these headphones are for you because once you get the SR80s tuned properly, the sound these cans deliver is very impressive. Very. Impressive.

Unfortunately, when using an IOS device, playing this profile with even high end earbuds like the UE Triple Fis, the sound will be tinny, so toggling between the two modes by way of a shortcut would be a nice bonus, but as it stands I have to go deep into the preferences to change this setting. Therefore, I would only recommend these headphones if you intend to use them in a stationary location. Since these are very high resistance earphones (even higher than most loudspeakers for that matter) you really ought to get an headphone amplifier if you want these to shine.

One other issue is with the minimalist foam cup pads. While they are comfy, they do not block sound in or out whatsoever, so if you use them in a noisy office you will be annoyed at how loud you have to play these to drown out ambient noise. Also, your workmates will probably be annoyed by the bleed through. I ended up getting a different cup pad kit which is marginally better, but it changes the fit somewhat so it takes a little fiddling to get them to sit on your skull around your ears evenly. Otherwise, the headphones are incredibly comfortable as they are very lightweight, which is surprising considering the size of the driver. Grado has found the sweet spot between having a massive (and heavy) drive coil magnet and being featherweight, even if I might take issue with their choices about fidelity reproduction.

Tl;DR: If you really like your sound overcharged with bass, these are the headphones for you. Otherwise, if you are looking for a quality but moderately priced pair of headphones, you might be better off with a more reference-style set like the Sony MDRs.

We just went through the worst winter storm in recorded history, down here in Austin Texas. In fact, it's still not over. Power is still out in a lot of areas. And, they're still doing 'rolling blackouts', even in our neighborhood. One of the things that we really depended on, with no power, no cell service, no internet, no NOTHING, was having this NOAA-AM-FM radio that was rechargeable by either cranking it yourself or solar panel. To be honest, I have THREE of these things. One in my truck, her car, and here at home. Some may say that I'm a worry wart. But, I say, better to have it and not need it....

This one, from the YEZRO Store took me a minute to figure out. It's a little different from the others. But, once I finally got it, it's really easy to operate. The flashlight is just bright enough to light your way in a dark house. (Don't expect it to light your path down a long dark road in the country.) The 'alarm' is more amusing than anything. (Really, I laughed.) The tuning knob is DIRECT on a very small tuner. So, you have to go SLOW when scrolling through the band for the best signal. The speaker is kind of small and tinny sounding. It has a battery level indicator LED that does a decent job of letting you know when it's time to recharge. The band selector switch works very well, as does the volume knob. You should know that the telescoping antenna is another way of getting the strongest signal from your chosen station. Radio signals travel up and down the antenna in a 'sign wave', not just to the tip. So, after you do your best with the tuning knob, you can increase or decrease the length of the radial (as well as change the angle) to fine tune it even more. This radio is NOT water proof. So, protect it from rain. The ability to play music from an SD card or a flash drive is a nice feature. But, I consider that kind of pointless in an 'emergency' radio.

I know that I've picked it apart quite a bit. But, looking at the primary function of this radio, and how well it served me in this winter storm, I can really only give it accolades. It did an admirable job. Especially considering the small investment I made in it. I'm glad I have it. And, now, it's going back in it's box and in my closet until the next storm. it gives me a sense of security, just knowing it's there.

It's a beautiful laptop, 17"x11" shut, the screen is huge, 17" measured diagonally. This is NOT a small laptop. It looks tough, almost tactical, with battleship-like lines and a somewhat menacing dark grey color.

The presentation or unboxing is sensational: it comes in a kind of large dark grey cardboard suitcase complete with handle. You open the box and there is the laptop along with two small rectangular insets in the top part of the box. No clutter, no plastic bags, even the power cable (which is also huge) is nestled, hidden, in a compartment near the hinge of the box.

Setup is magnificent and smooth as can be, a real delight. Nothing clunky about it, a genuine pleasure. The keyboard is enormous and includes a full numeric keypad to the right. The trackpad is (oddly) centered below the keyboard, not centered on the body and features two mouse-click areas below it.

The sound is as good as a laptop is going to have, which is somewhat tinny with no bass. You will want a set of external speakers. I had a Windows 7 home built computer which I stole a $10 set of Logitech speakers from which provided more than adequate sound.

The keyboard, function keys, Alienware logo and top and front lights are all PROGRAMMABLE, meaning you can set not only customized keystroke functions for the function keys, but set detailed COLORS for all of the elements to dream up customizable schemes, which sounds goofy but looks *awesome*. This is a gorgeous laptop from top to bottom, stem to stern. Easily the nicest laptop I've ever seen.

Would you use this for business? As in tote it to a business meeting? Probably not, you know, it looks great, but it's not business-drab styled. It's meant for gaming, and it truly rocks at that.

The screen has nearly unbelievable saturation and brightness, the colors almost drip off the screen, they're so rich. The tactical sensation of the keyboard is outstanding, it's not a mechanical "click" keyboard but rather the standard sensation with buttery-smooth Rolls-Royce operation. There is no optical drive, but that doesn't really matter these days. I was able to download a copy of Painter Essentials which would not run on my Mac, which ran great on the Alienware laptop.

I downloaded a trial copy of Illustrator and put it through its paces, the laptop had no trouble with anything I could throw at it. Plenty of RAM, no heating problems, a battery which lasts quite a long time uncoupled from shore power.

In short, the laptop is outstanding -- fantastic. Second to none. Beautifully designed, faster than any other laptop I've ever seen with a display better than any desktop computer I've ever used. The sound is weak, but it's impossible to squeeze decent speakers into that form factor -- external speakers or headphones are required. Software on board will support any sound system you want to add. It's all ready to roll and buffed like a body builder. Incredible!

And now, gentle reader, I need to address the sole problem I had with the Alienware laptop, and it's a big one: it ships with Windows 8.1.

The killer part of this is that having a gorgeous laptop like this with Win 8.1 is like having a yacht when you live in the desert. One doesn't really function without the other. I found Windows 8.1 impossible to use, it simply made no sense to me. Windows would pop up I never asked for, navigation was absurdly difficult -- it made no sense to me on a fundamental level. I was not a fan of Windows before, but Windows 7 on my homebrew game box functioned and was comprehensible to me, things MADE SENSE.

But Windows 8? I ran across a video critique (http://dottech.org/94027/this-hilarious-video-explains-why-windows-8-sucks-video/) of the interface and the fundamental flaws built into it -- one has to be curious what Microsoft was thinking. The interface choices simply make no sense. Why would they release such a horrible dog of an operating system?! I'm not a n00b when it comes to computers. And I could not make heads or tails out of Windows 8.1, which soured my experience with the Alienware laptop. Here we have a laptop which is outrageously powerful with a gorgeous display and an OS which I don't have anything good to say about. It's awful, truly, honestly awful.

My point being that if you want to get anything DONE with this laptop, beware Windows 8. If you're happy with getting your favorite games set up and playing those, then you'll be satisfied. For example, you're expected to enter or create a new e-mail account in order to proceed -- well, that I did, and in the month I've been trying to use this laptop, I've NEVER gotten the Microsoft e-mail account to function properly! Internet Explorer is included, and it's kind of buggy and suffers from the computer either changing programs or bringing up windows I never asked for ALL THE TIME. It's maddening. I'm not exaggerating or joking -- this thing is a train wreck, a real crazymaker.

Why not ship this laptop with some flavor of Linux? Or cobble together a Dell version of an OS? Windows 8 really is that bad. You can imagine the frustration of an OS that is the equivalent of an insane person on your laptop. Your beautiful, perfect laptop. It would have been great if there was a simple downgrade path to Windows 7. Or XP, or Win95 -- seriously, it's THAT BAD.

OK, enough of that. The OS is not Alienware's fault, but it does greatly interfere with the use of the laptop. Perhaps you'll have a better experience. For me, it was a major stumbling block EVERY TIME I TURNED THE LAPTOP ON. Absolute endless frustration. I just cannot figure out what Microsoft was thinking.

So, to sum up: this is the best laptop I've ever seen, absolutely ideal for gaming, and the other "serious" programs I got to run on it all performed beautifully. You will want to add external speakers and possibly an external CD/DVD drive if you need one. There are plenty of USB ports and the other sockets you expect. Support for sound is outstanding.

But the Windows 8 OS is like a rock in your shoe which makes every single step you take painful. With a different OS, this may well be the PERFECT laptop for personal gaming use. Absolutely gorgeous!
