The BOIFUN Portable Monitor really IS portable. It’s not that much bigger than my 13-inch MacBook Pro, and it weighs less. I could see packing the monitor for a trip, to use for work and play. I have used the monitor with my Mac and my Nintendo Switch, and it works great with both devices.

The monitor has USB-C and Mini HDMI input options. It comes with cables for both options, which I appreciated. That’s one small downside, you’ll need to make sure to take the Mini HDMI cable with you.

I used the USB-C input with my Mac, it worked. I used the Mini HDMI to HDMI input for my Nintendo Switch, it worked. With both devices, the picture on the monitor was clear and bright. The monitor is plug and play, no instructions really needed.

I did some online Splatoon matches with my Switch to see if there would be any noticeable lag or freezing on the monitor, there were no problems. The game looked great, although the built-in speakers are very tinny.

I do have a few complaints about the monitor. The “smart cover” is super basic. The pictures show folding the cover and using it as a stand, propping the monitor against it. Like a tablet smart cover. But that’s seemingly impossible to do. The cover is very floppy, with no support to hold itself in any stand-shape. The box does include a basic plastic stand, but I wish I could use the cover as pictured, since the stand is one more thing to pack if I go somewhere.

Also, the cover is like a file folder. There’s no way to attach it to the monitor. It relies on magnets alone to stay in place. I wish it had some sort of clip or strap inside, to secure the monitor.

Secondly, the input ports are on opposite sides. The USB-C port is on the same side as the power port, but the Mini HDMI port is on the other side. So if you want to use the monitor in landscape position, you’re limited by input type.

The monitor is powered via USB-C, a cable and wall adapter are included. The wall adapter is a basic 5V USB-A wall adapter. I like that it isn’t some proprietary charging cable.

I like the sleek appearance of the Monster Verse Wireless Earbuds. I have them in Black; the finish is matte black, on earbuds and case. I also like physical buttons on the “head” of each earbud, which you can use to adjust the volume, skip tracks, and answer/reject phone calls.

Unfortunately, the sound quality doesn’t live up to the sleek look. The sound is average, or a bit below. I’m not an audiophile, but I noticed that all songs I listened to were lighter than they should be, like I was listening through a blanket or muffler. Not so bad to be tin-can sounding, but the songs just weren’t punchy and true to how I know they should sound. Bass didn’t really exist. I notice the subpar sound quality even when watching a tv show or movie.

The earbuds don’t last very long, about 2-3 hours. The case does give an hour’s worth of playback with a 15 minute charge, which is handy in a pinch. I do wish the case had a better indicator to show how much battery life it has left, it just has one LED light.

The USB charging cable Monster included is super nice. It’s a braided cable with an adapter, to accommodate USB-C and USB-A. The case also supports wireless charging.

Comfort-wise, the earbuds come with 5 extra sets of tips in a blister pack. The earbuds have medium tips on, and then you have the option of small or large. I have a daith piercing in one ear, some earbuds are comfortable and some are not. For me, these are not. But the earbuds can be used independently, so I usually wear one if I use them.

I think the sound quality on the bopmen S40 Active Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Headphones is pretty good. I’m not an audiophile, but my ears know what they like. These headphones provide smooth playback; they don’t sound tinny or like I’m listening from far away.

The Active Noise Cancelling is about as good as noise cancelling I have on Sony headphones. I live with my mom and she watches videos that drive me crazy. So the bopmen headphones have saved my sanity for the last month. The ANC mutes enough of the loud background noise of her videos that I can get some work done.

The headphones are made from plastic and feel solid. They fold up for travel; I don’t feel like they’re going to break in my bag. The box includes a pouch for storage/travel.

The ear cups are a bit smaller than I would expect for over ear headphones. The earmuffs are some sort of leatherette material that is soft, with pretty good cushioning. If I wear the headphones for more than 2 to 3 hours at a time, I do start to get a headache from the squeeze and fit.

These are really secure. I paired them with my phone, and then with my [[ASIN:B06XCWLL12 All-New Kindle Oasis E-reader - 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers]] I then lost the Kindle (it's in the house - I see it on my WiFi network, just not with my eyes) and paired it with yet another Kindle. So it can handle three paired devices no issue.

The point of pairing sports earphones with a Kindle was to listen to an audiobook while running on the treadmill. I'm a sort of "bouncy" runner. It's a problem I'm working on. But I usually use headphones rather than earbuds, because of that, and because, even when I'm not bouncing, I'm pretty hit or miss with ear buds. I have more problems with them falling out than most of my friends do. I just kind of suck with them for some reason. Anyway, these don't fall out, even with the bouncing.

They sound great for audiobooks, for GraphicAudio novels (which are kind of a blend between audio book and old style radio drama) and for music. They don't get tinny at the extremes of pitch.

The only thing I dislike about these is that the control is so high near the ear it's hard to use without taking the earbud out. That and my cat keeps trying to run off with them, but that's another story. I should point out, they have survived multiple cat attacks.

This was incredibly easy to pair. I paired it with my Kindle Fire HDX and it was faster than any Bluetooth pairing I've ever done before.

The sound quality is astounding. If I put it on the hardwood floor, and if I play something with a lot of base, and it I turn it up about half way, it will shake the floor. The range is equally impressive. It does not go tinny on the high notes. The sound remains clean and clear at all volumes (or did until my neighbor came to yell at me to turn it down). It produces music of a quality one would expect from a full sized unit.

The only thing to be aware of is that the speakers are along both long sides. That makes for fantastic sound, but the device must stand on the short edge while in use, which to my mind is not as stable. It uses a proprietary charger rather than charging via USB. Makes it just a tiny bit less convenient, but not a big thing. That's all I can say against it.

Unboxing: It came in a nice long box, well packaged. It comes with a fat instruction booklet. I was absolutely shocked to find out it wasn't just useless legal drivel. There's 70 pages of useful, illustrated, and well written text. There's also a paper wall mount template so you can get your holes easily drilled in the right place. They've included an HDMI cable. I try to use the cables that come with things first lately instead of what I already had. The cords themselves are often only rated up to a certain level of capability. There's also a headphone style audio cord, a power cord, two very solid mounting brackets, a remote control with batteries, and a quick start guide.

The speaker itself is impressive. It's big, long, and heavy. Looks and feels like a high quality piece of equipment. I'm putting it on my mantle rather than wall mounting it. The power cord is a bit short. That's fair I guess. extension cords can make it longer, but extra loops of cord can be hard to deal with. The cord is a fairly standard two prong with 8 shaped end. Unfortunately, there is no real thought put towards cable management. There's a notch in back where the cords plug in, but no channel they can run in, so the speaker needs to be a cord's width away from the wall unless you're going to drill a hole right there or something. At least the end of the cord is smallish, so that's viable.

I do have a Sony Bravia television with a center (behind the screen) speaker, which this soundbar is designed to take advantage of. I wired things up as described in the instructions, and was getting video but not audio. What I ended up figuring out is that I needed to have my devices hooked up to the speaker inputs and then it would send the video signal to the television, which is the opposite of the old days when the television cords went out to the speakers. There are only three HDMI jacks on this, and one may be needed for the ARC channel to a television. Just enough for my needs, but I think splitters should work though if you have more devices.

It does a very quick and inoffensive sound check to analyze the room acoustics and adjust accordingly. The remote is refreshingly extensive, with things like separate volume buttons for rear speakers and subwoofer. So many speakers these days either don't give you the options, or have them deep in the menus somewhere. Sometimes I just want to crank up the bass for a rocket launch or something. Doesn't mean I want to listen to it rumble through a financial report. I don't have the rear speakers or the subwoofer yet, but I think I'm going to have to pick them up.

I've tried a lot of speakers over the years, including some recent ones just below this price range, and this one is a keeper. It's got great sound. Very immersive, not tinny. It sounds like a lot of good sized speakers. I'm so glad to see companies starting to put out surround sound systems with wireless rear/subwoofers. The big soundbar too. It's such a relief to be able to do this without having to run wires everywhere, and to have it automatically adjust to room acoustics. It handles bluetooth as well, USB, hooks up to wifi, and works with smart assistants.

I really love this speaker. I already have two sets of Bose earbuds, so I already had the Bose app downloaded to my phone. It was easy to pair and didn't have any issues getting set up. I don't control it through the app, I just control it through the buttons on the speaker itself or just by turning the music on my phone on or off.

I wanted a simple speaker that I didn't need to worry too much about so that I could listen to podcasts and music in the shower, or when working in my vegetable greenhouse this summer. So far it's been great! The battery life has been longer than expected, the sound quality is absolutely amazing for listening to music and has great bass, not any kind of tinny sound at all, and the unit itself seems thoughtfully designed and built to last. It's got a nice weight to it and doesn't want to tip over.

I really appreciate after having a bunch of Chinese made brands in the past, that this one is just straight up quality, everything works, it's easy to deal with, etc.

I haven't truly tested the water resistant capability of it, but after two weeks of showering with it just outside the shower and bringing it into the sometimes drippy or humid greenhouse, it still doing great.

Overall the Bose quality shines through in this item and I've been really thrilled with it for my purposes.

These headphones offer crisp sound with deep bass capability, and decent treble that can *sometimes sound slightly tinny but isn’t a big deal. The noise cancellation works great on a wide range of white noise, from the fridge or dishwasher to airplane engines. The fit is comfortable for short or long use, and the package includes a travel bag. Important note on cables: DO NOT LOSE THE AUX CABLE—it converts the usbc to an auxiliary standard headphone/sound jack. THERE IS NO STANDARD AUX SOUND SOUND JACK ON THE HEADPHONES. Just remember your cable and it will be fine, but it only has one port for both charging and listening. Great headphones!

This is WAY too big. Even when you adjust it to the maximum tightness. It moved around all night and kept me up, so I won’t be using it again. The sound was tinny, which I sort of expected. It’s ok for podcasts, but I wouldn’t use it for music—the sound quality just isn’t there. Pretty design, with nice, giftable packaging, but the product itself just didn’t work out at all. Note: if you’re a side sleeper, this will be particularly uncomfortable—you can feel the plastic insert of the speakers on either side.

These low-profile, lightweight earbuds have some decent active noise canceling that helps drown out white noise like air conditioners, fans, airplane engines, etc. There are 3 options for the rubber buds at the end, with the smallest working ok for a decent fit. (The others were HUGE)
As for sound quality, these are a solid choice, especially considering the price point. The treble is crisp and not tinny, unlike many earbuds, and the bass is strong and pretty powerful. Good sound definition and clarity, plus a transparent mode to be able to hear your surroundings.
Overall: solid in all categories, and reasonably priced for good quality Bluetooth earbuds!

These headphones are a solid value for what you get. Below are highlights of various features and drawbacks:
Excellent:
-active noise cancelling
-clarity/definition of sound
-carrying case comfort
Very good:
-audio for podcasts and tv
Ok:
-treble is a *little on the tinny side
-bass isn’t as deep or powerful as I’d like

This is great for exercise, sports, and regular use, with comfort and a good fit with 3 size options. For phone calls? Not so good at all. The interface is also too complicated and there are numerous miscommunications. Nice sound! See below for details:
Pros:
-nice, relatively compact case (for over-ear)
-buds sit securely in place with a different design than many over-ear buds
-light and comfortable
-resists sweat and some (light) rain
-nice, clear sound with good definition
-strong enough bass to enjoy music
-treble sounds clear and not tinny
-comfortable even with glasses—some other similar buds have issues
-no issues while wearing face masks—stays out of the way pretty well
Cons:
-somewhat overwhelming instruction manual with tiny pics…normally not an issue, except that…
-the touch interface is not great. Where exactly do I touch this thing? How long do I touch exactly? (the manual says, but it doesn’t always interpret it the way I intended) Why does it work sometimes and not others? I prefer buttons for this instead of working out this strange elusive code. Not thrilled.
-just ok for phone calls…sound is fine either side, but hanging up happens WAY too easily when adjusting volume. I tapped Super quickly, and it thought that would work, but it interpreted this as “hang up”…and it does this often.
-just adjusting these causes you to “press” or activate a function. In the case of phone calls, just lightly touching to adjust means hanging up

If these were in a lower price point, they’d have more stars, but for the current price of ~$80, there’s a problem that really should not be there: a very high pitch whine in the background. It’s noticeable most when you have noise cancelling on with silence in the background, or in sections of music or voice that are quiet. It’s not terribly loud, but I can pick it up from time to time.
Other than that, the noise cancelling is pretty good, and the sound has good clarity and power. The treble isn’t super tinny the way some headphones are—EXCEPT when you bring the volume up. THEN, it does get tinny, and the bass doesn’t have quite the power you might like. You can hear subtle details in most music, which I appreciate, and pairing is easy.
As for comfort, the ear cups are a bit small and have a somewhat awkward fit, though they are lightweight and reasonably comfortable.
All in all, these would be Great headphones if they were in the $40-$50 range. In the $80 range, they’re just ok.

The sound quality on these is excellent across the board:
*high definition: you will hear every detail from breathing and clothing moving, to the sound of a violin stroke changing direction in the orchestra
*powerful bass: listening to a deep beat is excellent with these
*crisp treble: not tinny, just crisp and clear

The smart pause stops your music when you take the headphones off, so interruptions don’t make you lose your place, whether for podcasts or music.

Pairing was easy, and there are lots of controls on the headphones so you can use them for calls, Siri, dictation, etc..

USB-C: these headphones are compatible with my new MacBook pro, but if you do not have anything with USB-C, this includes an adapter for USB-C to standard USB. The last thing one wants to do is drop more money just to charge these, so it’s good they included this to make it portable and usable.

Speaking of portability, the carry case is soft, which means it won’t protect the headphones well. This looked cheaper than I expected, especially considering that I own significantly cheaper headphones than these with a better case. It might seem petty to point this out, but part of having noise cancelling headphones is usually because you travel and want to block the noise of an airplane, train, or ship engine out. If the case isn’t good for travel, then it’s a problem, and you have to figure out another way to pack these, whether that means buying something that is not a great fit for the size, or just risking it.

I’m used to a more clear button system, so I worried when I put these on that my phone wouldn’t find them, yet they did! It paired quickly and easily without any problems, and the sound had surprisingly good definition, allowing subtle sounds to come through. Even so, the treble could have been a little less tinny and the bass a bit stronger. Likewise, there was some slight distortion for some volumes and sounds. It wasn’t often, but it happened with enough songs that I had to remark on it. These are good, not great headphones. Now taking price into account, they are Way better than expected! For under $30, these are pretty great Bluetooth headphones.

I’ve tested hundreds of products, and it’s not often they arrive broken out of the box, but this one sure did, and I saw some other reviews with the same issue. These are cheap and unreliable. They look awesome and are basically a toy. You get what you pay for, but not even that in this case. I expected tinny not awesome speakers, but I thought they would at least work. Nope. Not with the headphone jack, and not with the USB. Do Not Buy.

Always taking price points into account and comparing within the range (as well as referring to the high end products for where the relevant technology currently is), these are pretty great!
Note that many headphones say “noise cancelling” and actually mean that they insulate against outside sounds through earplugs or other physical barriers muffling outside noise, as opposed to actively using other sound waves to sort of cancel out many frequencies, which is a powered process requiring technology that can listen, identify, and then send appropriate sounds at all times to create this quieting effect.
Ok, so knowing that ACTIVE noise cancelling is usually a high end thing found in Bose and similar products for $300-$500, seeing a $50~ product offer this is pretty neat!
And for the price, it’s pretty good, and so is the sound! While slightly canned and tinny on the treble, a common problem on mid or lower end headphones, it is still great for the price and has nice features!
Good!

Considering you get a separate lightning to aux adapter, which purchased separately is around $8-9, what you are buying is basically some decent $10 headphones with a nice compact carrying case and replacement/alternate sized earbuds. Considering the price point and what is included, these are nice! The treble is a bit tinny and the bass is not particularly strong, but that's to be expected for something on a budget. They're powerful enough and good enough for phone calls, podcasts and the like, and if you're not picky about music, they're *ok* for this too. Me? I'm kind of an audio snob, so I would only use it for talk. Not bad!

The detail on these headphones is mind-blowingly good! Wow!
These are just as good as my Bose headphones, offering such quality sound that you can hear a violin's bow touch the strings the moment before they vibrate and sing. You can hear clothing and breath in chamber music and spoken word. Every single aspect of your audio comes across clearly.
Exquisite for every genre of music, you can expect strong, powerful bass, crisp treble that is clear and not tinny at all. The impressive design is also versatile, with wires for headphone jacks, USB, or bluetooth capacity, all providing excellent quality for any music or spoken word. They're my new favorites.
Side note, and I know this is not important at all, but the packaging is gorgeous, to the point I felt bad throwing it out and will probably turn the cardboard box into some kind of clutch! haha
I'd never heard of this brand, but I'll remember V-Moda now! Exquisite! I HIGHLY recommend these!

If you take the insulated thermos/bottle, detach it from the speaker, and throw the speaker out, you'd have a great product at an insanely high price. And that's basically where you are with this: the bottle does its job perfectly, offering a drink that stays hot or cold for hours, with a loop at the top to hang it or carry it conveniently with a carabiner. Everything in that department is fine, until you add the speaker.

Ease of use: great for both halves. Fits most standard cup holders, has the loop, unscrews from speaker to make it washable and versatile for when you don't want horrible sound shooting out the bottom half.

Appearance: really cool! It's a great concept, and you're probably less likely to have this speaker stolen because it looks like a regular drinking bottle from afar. Nice for the beach (partly because ambient noise makes the sound quality tolerable).

Sound quality: the worst. It's like $5 earbuds, but much louder. It is extremely tinny, whether attached or detached from the bottle, with incredibly weak bass that is almost inaudible, and shrill treble. The low and high ends come together to create a perfect cacophony of undefined sounds making every genre of music sound awful. Like iTunes played on your speaker phone, your music will sound the same but louder.

Value: I'd pay $15-$20 max for this. The sound quality really ruins what was a cool concept.

3.5 stars taking price into account

With headphones, it is always a blend of "you get what you paid for", and comparing to others at a similar price point.
How do these compare? Well, they are about average for the $20-$40 range. Not much better, not much worse. And as is the case with headphones, for a bit more, you can do MUCH better, and for a bit less, you will get roughly similar results. (In other words, headphones under $75-$100 are, more or less very similar, and then suddenly, your options get drastically better.)

Here's my analysis on the general sound quality and other features:

MISC:
Phone calls: 5 stars: Easy to use, works great for calls on both ends, and blocks outside sound quite well!
Ease of use/pairing: 5 stars: It passed the test of not having to read instructions, meaning it is incredibly simple to pair and use
Appearance: 5 stars: Neat! It's colorful and fun, as well as practical and functional!
External noise: 4 stars: Because it has a pretty tight seal, it is like an earplug, blocking outside sound quite effectively
Comfort: 3 stars: comparable to others of this design. Totally fine at first, and annoying after long use.

SOUND:
Treble: 2 stars: quite tinny
Bass: 2 stars: ok depth, not great, not very powerful
Overall: 2 stars: not much detail in the sound, but it can get pretty loud without distorting, and it is definitely good enough for basic listening and phone calls. There also appears to be a *very slight* hiss in quiet/silent moments when the volume is louder.

OVERALL:
The average is 28 out of 40 possible points, or 70% (a "C" grade, if it were going to school ;-), but because the above analysis does not take price point into account, comparing this to brands like Bose, as well as dollar store headphones, this means that for the current list price of roughly $29.99, this is a reasonable expectation.

The average number of stars based on my rubric is 3.5 stars: decent for this price point, and certainly good enough to enjoy music and spoken word, and to have successful phone calls.

Between the perfect fit of the earbuds and the detailed full-range sound, these headphones create an immersive sound experience.
The bass is deep and powerful, and the treble is crisp and clear—not tinny like many headphones. The sound is detailed and clear enough to allow the listener to hear ambient sounds in the recording like breath or clothing (depending on the particular track, of course), so one can pick up fairly subtle elements and enjoy music with both very quiet and quite loud parts. Likewise, it’s great for radio and podcasts because voices and words sound defined.

And the setup?
Well, it passed my “can I make this happen without a manual or instructions” test. I didn’t open the booklet, and that was fine! Turn on Bluetooth, press the button between the volume buttons for a bit, it shows up, and bam. You’re ready to go. So far, I haven’t needed to read anything—it works and is straightforward.

Phone calls?
Fine! Just like the wired headphones but wireless—no issues!

This is a pretty mixed review of an interesting concept that is pretty good right now, but has the potential to be great in the near future. At the current price of about $150, this is ok+ based on the following criteria:

Sound Quality: 2.5-3 stars
For the size, it's ok
When reviewing for sound quality, I compare speakers (and headphones) to comparably sized items, based on speakers I currently or previously have owned. I take price range *somewhat* into account (I don't expect $15 headphones to sound like $500 ones), but for anything over $100, I use the full range from the cheapest stuff I have, to my favorite brand, Bose.
So with that in mind, I have a portable wireless Bose speaker that is smaller and acts as the "5" on the scale.
The sound on this can get loud enough to not distort and still fill a smallish room or normal bedroom fine. The treble and bass are ok, though the higher ranges are tinny and the bass lacks depth. Overall sound from high to low and throughout the mid range lack definition. It's good enough for very casual background listening and for podcasts.

Alexa Feature: 4 stars
I have an iPhone and think Alexa has quite a bit more understanding and skill than Siri. When asked questions, from simple stuff like "what's the weather" to more complicated stuff like "I'm hungry. What can I make in half an hour?", the answers and follow-up questions are highly intuitive and thorough. Does she get everything all the time? No. But she does a much better job than Siri.

User-Friendliness: 2.5 stars
I didn't like the process of figuring out how this works, particularly the part of pairing with more than one device and also Having to use an app to make most of it work. It was a clunky, irritating process that more or less stayed that way every time I wanted to use this thing, especially for listening to music. It should be able to just play from your iTunes through the iTunes app and bluetooth, and instead, I was only able to make it play iTunes though Their App, which sucks when it comes to my music. And that brings us to the App..

App: 2 stars
No. Just no. Bluetooth exists for a reason, and if a speaker has bluetooth, you should be able to just pair and play. I had to use the app to play from my iTunes, and because I have a very specific way of organizing things, I was incredibly annoyed that something didn't translate, and my music was disorganized and basically impossible to search for with this app. Instead of being able to play what I want from one of my playlist subfolders, it disregarded my way of organizing things, and I ended up giving up. If I can't listen to my stuff easily with this, then like 75% of the reason to use this disappears, leaving me with an expensive alarm clock with weather report, recipe ideas, and some cool internet stuff. That's cool, but it's quite incomplete for what I need, and what I suspect many people want.

tl;dr version: sound is mediocre but doable, app is bad, Alexa is super clever and smart, and the experience has a lot of frustrating aspects.

Bear in mind that as gaming headphones, the sound quality is not as suited for other applications like listening to music. Having said that, here's how the experience went:

Appearance: maybe this is some macho thing, but they are enormous and intense-looking in an almost exaggerated way. So if you're one of those people that likes huge flashy stuff or ostentatiously masculine-looking things, this is perfect? They're huge.

Comfort: Very comfy! The cup part is large and fits great, and the headband adjusts nicely to most average head sizes. The microphone is fully adjustable, making it work for anyone.

Sound blocking: pretty good! While it does not use noise-cancelling technology, the sheer size and generous build of the headphones allows for Very effective sound cancellation. I had my partner listen to something with her back to me so she could not see me, and with the volume turned up, I had to full on Scream for her to hear me.

Sound quality: Better for spoken word and voices, honestly. The sound is crisp and detailed, but it's also a little canned-sounding, with somewhat sharp, tinny trebles and less-than-intense bass. This does best in mid-range and capturing voices and sounds, and less so for actual music. Having said that, it is certainly better than cheap headphones for music, so it does have some versatility if you're not too picky.

Overall: These are pretty great! They even have an adapter that can be used by other devices that unites the audio input and output, which comes split for certain applications like computers or other gaming. (Meaning, theres a separate cable for the microphone and audio input, and they come with an adapter to have a single "female" connection that can work on phones or other single-plug devices using audio in/out.)

Cool!

There are some pretty neat features with these headphones that make them uniquely better for some people. For example, if you are slightly hard of hearing (but do not use/need a hearing aid), these can actually turn the world around you up, making it a bit louder to better hear conversations. Likewise, you can turn the world down and make things more quiet!

The charging and holding case is also pretty awesome! They live and charge in this neat little box that indicates when it is charging or ready to pair, a process that was relatively easy, but sometimes buggy when putting on and taking off.

For music, you get a nice amount of detail in the sound. I always test it with orchestral music to see if you can pick up on the gentle rustle of clothing. Yes, you can hear that! At the same time, however, the sound can be a *little* tinny and lack richness among the treble notes. Overall, the quality for music is good. Not amazing, not mediocre or bad. Just a solid good.

For audio, it is excellent--crisp, clearly-defined sound!

And yes, you can make phone calls with these!

They take a little troubleshooting to figure out, but they're well worth the effort for their many interesting features. Cool technology!

These super comfortable headphones have special cushioning that helps block out extraneous noise, so while they may not be noise-cancelling, they do a great job making the outside world fade away. (It is not the standard cup-type design with a hollowed out section with a puffy circular exterior--the whole thing is cushioned, kind of like an extra-squishy ear ottoman!)

The sound itself is good. Not amazing, but very good. (There is a hint of tinny quality to treble, and the bass notes are not super super intense.) But I am a musician and dancer, so I am more critical than most on this. For regular usage, for people not super invested in extreme detail or the highest quality, these are awesome.

Note: I was not able to activate sharing between other bluetooth brands and these. I am pretty sure you need more than one of this exact brand for the sharing feature to work. That's another thing to consider, along with the fact you would have to double your investment (current price is $199, so not particularly cheap).

Great headphones with a cool sharing feature, if your other pair is of the same kind.

4.5 stars
While the treble may leave something to be desired, with a rather tinny quality and slight general lack of detail in overall sound, these headphones are decent! The bass is strong and doesn't distort, and best of all, the fit is excellent. It holds well and is very comfortable, both on its own, as well as in comparison to other similar products.
Easy setup and pairing, too! Nice headphones, especially for modern music that emphasizes bass sounds. Solid workout option!

The buds are ok, though with small ears, they don't stay in great. As for the sound, it could be better, especially for the price. The overall quality sounds rather tinny, and it lacks detail in general and strength on the low and high ends.

I would have liked to see better sound quality and fit for this product. It's ok, but for the money, I expected a bit more.

The main issue I have with headphones is usually the fit, then secondly, the tendency for the sound to be tinny. But this is Bose.

Known for innovative and exemplary sound quality, Boss speakers and headphones are consistently top-of-the-line, and these are no exception to that expectation. The high and low ends remain clear, crisp, and defined, free of distortion of echo, maintaining detail in whatever you are listening to, whether orchestral or spoken word, hip hop or show tunes. Everything sounds great!

As for fit, that is also great! They stay in perfectly and block out noise quite well, and I can dance with them without problems for the most part. That's a first!

These are excellent. But if you've heard of Bose, this won't be a surprise.

I thought by the look and price of it that this would be an excellent sound system. Well, it is portable, very easy to use and pair, and looks fantastic....but the sound quality is terrible. The bass, even at a lowish volume, sounds distorted and fuzzy, creating a Lot of vibration and very little in terms of quality sound. For the higher end, it sounds tinny, as though coming through a can. Meanwhile, the overall detail in the sound is poor, creating a fuzzy output that makes nearly any genre of music sound flat. I have speakers a tenth this size that sound better. I would not recommend it.

While they are ok for the price in terms of sound quality, fit, and durability, they lack a fundamental function for what Many people use to play their music: the ability to receive and make phone calls. If you are using a smartphone, these are only headphones, not headphones with a function button (like the kind that come with an iPhone, for example), and not ones that have an output through which you can speak or take dictation.
That aside, the sound quality was ok, with a somewhat tinny, canned quality and poor capability in processing deep bass or treble. If changing the levels to decrease treble, you'll see some improvement in the sound. For anything spoken word like podcasts, these are fine.
The fit is not bad. Usually, these things are big on me (female with apparently small ear-holes, if you would judge by most headphones), but these were comfortable. The three sizes of rubbery earplugs always help and are generally standard, and the ear hooks also aide in keeping them in place.

Summary:
For the price, you get decent headphones that do not have an output function.

The concept of building degrees of surround sound is pretty cool--nice use of bluetooth, and had the sound quality been better, it would probably be a worthwhile investment since it works with every device I have tried it with (iPhone, iPad, a few laptops). The initial setup isn't quite as straightforward as pressing a button and waiting for it to show on the other device's screen, but it's not horrible either; it just requires a little reading in the instruction book. Once paired, the devices find themselves easily and it's no longer an issue.
As for the sound, it's a little tinny and doesn't carry as far as other brands in my home (Pioneer and Bose), and considering this one isn't that much cheaper, it might be worthwhile paying the extra hundred or so dollars for one of the leading brands; however, the fact these can be paired with each other to create surround sound does make a compelling argument for buying them.
Interesting and useful product with decent but not excellent sound.

This is a simple device that does what it promises We were recently having work done on the house and the workers accessed the house via a back door. this alerted me to their comings and goings. It is easy to install and requires three AAA batteries that are not included. I found that anoying as this is neither an expensive or especially complex. There are two functions, a chime which notifies when someone enters or exits and an ear piercing alarm. You have 30 second to input a four digit pin to deactivate the alarm. Since the work has been completed, I am thinking of moving it to a back shed door. It is effective and works well.While certainly not a complete security system in and of itself, it can be a useful device to notify and alert.

I thought this would be ideal for my office, compact, portable and easy to use. If it had superior sound, so much the better. Unfortunately, it is adequate, not significantly superior to a clock radio you could buy at a discount department store.

On the plus size,, it is compact and light. It can use either batteries or electric and stands either horizontally or vertically. I was annoyed when I first received it that the release of the app had not yet occurred but set it up anyhow to use the speakers. While I wasn't expecting BOSE quality, I was hoping for something more than the tinny sound it emits. You can also play other mp3s, which is a nice feature. When the app is downloaded, the clock works and is easily readable. It is made of black plastic and is fairly inobtrusive.

This App Station is okay. It functions but is not in the least bit impressive in sound or quality. They remind me of the dollar store umbrellas I periodically buy for my office. They do the job without style or flair and if something happens to the, it doesn't break your heart.

My JBL Charge stopped taking a charge so I initially purchased the less expensive version of this Cambridge speaker to use with my Iphone 6. Sadly the sound was tinny and the bass was pretty much non-existant so I returned it and bought this model. Quite a difference. Maybe not as beefy as my JBL was, but for the price it is absolutely terrific.

It is cute, really small, extremely light, and simply perfect in the backyard, to the beach, at your desk or in a warehouse, or just about anywhere that you want good sound and don't want to take up too much space.

I keep mine in my bathroom so I can listen when I'm in the shower, in the tub, or just getting ready for work. The music sounds great and the volume is excellent without any distortion whatsoever. I'm also using it in the yard when reading or working on my plants.

I've only had it a couple of weeks so I don't know how it's going to work out with charging cause it's still going strong with daily use.

Time will tell - and I will update any changes - but for now I am very happy with this purchase.

I was very disappointed after reading so many positive reviews.

This unit was to be primarily used in my bathroom with my Iphone 6 while I get ready for work. It was to replace a JBL Charge I'd had for a few years and no longer would hold a charge.

The sound is strong, but tinny. No real depth or strong bass notes. I played several songs and really, really wanted it to work. Finally, I just gave up.

Now, the reason I gave it 2 stars is that it would be perfect for spoken-word use. It paired up fairly quick and the size is simply perfect for portability. And it is very attractive.

So I decided to give the Angle 3 Plus a shot for $7.00 more. Wow - what a difference! Sounds great, bass is perfect for the size, and I couldn't be happier.

Bottom line is that the choice is totally subjective on the part of the listener but, for the money, the Cambridge Angle 3 Plus is the way to go.

I was extremely skeptical upon receiving this speaker because I mean after all, it is a tiger head with the speakers located in the eye sockets. Okay. Then I plugged in my Iphone 4 - and played Evanescense, Ennio Morricone, and John Barry. Totally blown away.

I have owned portable speakers by Logitech, JBL, and Ihome - all very good, some a little better. My biggest complaint with them was that they were too large to drag in and out of the house and just not portable enough for my needs. But since I wanted good sound, I'd put up with the inconvenience. Till now.

I know you won't believe me because I can't even believe it myself, but this little speaker packs quite a wallop in the sound department. No need to adjust knobs for bass and treble (there aren't any), because the balance is excellent. Put in 3 triple A batteries, adjust your smart phone to the highest volume setting, plug it in the already attached adapter cord, and flip the little switch at the bottom of the tiger's head. There is a sliding volume control on the side of the head which you can then proceed to raise or lower according to your needs. That's it. The sound is rich and deep without the tinny trebble or heavy bass you get from other models. It even sounds terrific when I switch to my Pandora app.

The only drawback is that there is no where to plug in an adaptor for charging my smart phone. But big deal - now I can use my more expensive, bigger speakers to do that. Cause this little guy can be held in one hand along with my Iphone and I can go from room to room playing my music and setting it down anywhere I want.

Please give this little guy or one of the other animal heads a try. You'll be as surprised and thrilled as I was to discover such a cool, useful and perfect little speaker buddy.

UPDATE (4/2/13):

I've been using this speaker every single day since I got it. The sound is still amazing for such a small, clever design and the batteries seem to last longer than I'd originally believed. In fact, I'm so happy with this item, I've decided to place an order for the Panda version so I can have one of each in different parts of my home. I will review the Panda once I receive it, but I'm pretty confident it will be just as terrific as the tiger's been.

After owning 4 different pairs of earbuds (and test-driving a whole bunch more) since Christmas, these are absolutely without question the best product out there. They fit perfectly the first time I put them on, but without that feeling that you have added insulation to your ears. Other manufacturers misconstrue this as "noise reduction" when in fact everthing sounds muffled like you attached cotton balls to the earbuds.

I have been using these earbuds for over 2 hours non-stop - skipping between movies, t.v. shows, audiobooks and, of course, music. The sound is clear but not tinny. Everything sounds rich and warm without being overwhelming. They are extremely comfortable and blow away the original ones that came with my unit. For a while I began to think my ears were deformed because the original earbuds kept falling out (my husband said my ears were missing a piece). Now I know better.

The price is a little steep I agree. However, if you're gonna invest $249.00 or however much in an Ipod and heaven knows how much more in downloads, than it would only stand to reason that you would want the best sound possible. Otherwise, why bother owning one in the first place?

These are simply terrific and I hope everyone out there who has ears as apparently deformed as mine will go and buy a pair. You will be ecstatic with the results.
Quality isn’t bad for something this small sounds a bit “tinny” but works. Battery life is about 2 hours, it does not hold a charge. I have to charge it every day for work.
You get what you pay for. Not bad for the price, I needed something quick for work, it needed to be small enough for my gym bag. It has a bit of a “tinny” sound but will serve its purpose for now.

I bought a pair of these years ago and have always loved them. I needed another set of earbuds for travel, so I bought some less expensive ones...which sounded tinny...and another not-so-cheap set that sounded flat...and finally just bought another set.

I have super-large ear canals, out of which all earbuds fall, but these stay neatly in place no matter what. They also don't hurt my ears. And the sound is sublime.

The wireless version is on my gift wishlist.

I got these for $40 at my local Best Buy and they are objectively pretty terrible compared to my previous $32 Sennheiser CX~s earbuds. The shiny material seems so much flimsier, almost as light as plastic, and the skullcandy logo is poorly integrated and a bit cheesy. The sound quality is tinny and poor -- it doesn't really exclude sound and doesn't give you as much of a surround feeling with lush deep notes. I feel like I'm practically listening to apple earbuds (except that they're a bit more comfortable). I'm afraid to yank too hard on it in case of compromising the inexpensive materials it's made of, and when I slide on a couch or something I get a lot of feedback from the earphones. Also, when I just plug it into the computer I hear a constant low buzz.

tl;dr not very good, even for the current $25 price. I'd spend an extra $10-20 to get something that sounds really good, and might last.

I was disappointed when I first played my iPad on the TDA7498E as the sound was very shallow, hollow, and tinny. I read the instructions and they say give this five to seven hours to break in. Sure enough the sound is now much warmer and I am totally satisfied with this $75 amp. Solid, metal construction.

Still figuring this out. But what I have seen so far, this is going to be great. Especially in my big, beautiful, newly renovated bathroom. No more tinny music from my phone or the cheesy little Bluetooth speaker I had.

I have finally got to digging through all the wires, plugs and pieces, and am attempting to read the instruction book, the thickness of a small magazine. I will update as soon as get it up and running. I wish I could post pictures, it is hard to describe, but it has a LAN plug-in, mini USB and a regular USB ports, the plug that your electrical line plugs in if running on ac not battery. It has a standard headphone jack, then it gets weird (for me), with another jack connector just like the headphone jack, that is labeled “optical in/analog in”. No idea about that one!

I am off to study the manual. Will update.

Update: there is not one scrap of paper with any kind of instructions on hooking it up, what all the oddball plugs and extra electrical wire with weird metal tipped outlet plug is for. This is absolutely ridiculous. I am going to have to search up info on the internet somewhere. Not all of us are electronics rain-man types.

The XClear Wireless Earbuds arrived in a nice Apple-like packaging. Included are the black rectangular charging case, left and right black earbuds, a short USB-C cable, and 3 various sized earcaps. For the price I did not expect much in terms of quality; however the plastic material has a nice matte feel to it. The angular exterior of the earbud pieces makes it stand apart from the Airpod.

Charging didn't take too long. My first impression wearing these was that they were very comfortable. I generally do not like earbuds but these are small enough that they don't cause pain after wearing them for a long time. Initially I thought the sound was a little tinny, however with a little adjustment I was able to get a better rich sound once the buds were properly seated in the canal. There's a definite lack of bass if you are into that.

Overall for the price I was very pleasantly surprised by the material and construction of the Xclear earbuds. Only time will tell if these will hold up but after testing for a few hours I can heartily give these two thumbs up!

I've had my fair share of IE monitors & over the ear headphones & as far as sound quality, imaging, sound stage, separation these are amazing. Bass was very present but not overwhelming. The highs were not sharp or sibilant at all. But when it came to the fit I couldn't get past 1/2 hour & I tried ALL of the tips, which FIIo does a great job of giving you plenty to chose from. But unfortunately for me these just killed my listening enjoyment.

This is a decent speaker with some nice touches, but only for those who listen to music occasionally and are fine with "good enough if I can hear it" sound. Details

Size: relative small footprint--bigger than a lot of better sounding bluetooth speakers, but also comes with extras so can't fault them on size.

Pairing: paired easily and immediately with all our IOS devices--phones and iPads, and our Mac laptops. Never lost signal

Clock: nice and bright, easy to read, easy to set

Q1 charge-worked with all our compatible devices with no problems at all, couldn't be easier to use

battery life about as promised--we went 6+ hours twice

dual speakers are distinguishable

The downside as noted at the top is sound. It isn't horrible--it's clear enough. But it's definitely thin if not tinny, and lacks a full, rich output/range. We have a Denon, a Jam, and a UE Boom, and all are noticeably, significantly better, richer, fuller sounding. (they obviously don't come with clocks or wireless charging).

that said, my wife thought his sounded "fine". It's all in your expectations and desires. I would not use this as a listening device; she'd be perfectly happy with it. So know where you are in the "how good does my music need to be and how often do I listen to it" spectrum

I'm not an audiophile, nor do I have fancy audio equipment to measure, compare, etc. I'm just a guy who likes music. So that that as you want. That said, not that I've finally managed to get these hookedup, I can say I"m super pleased.

The look is sleek and compact. The black will fit into any modernist style, not so much if you're more rustic/wood-based decor.

The sound is rich and clear, especially if one doesn't push volume super high. There isn't a deep low bass, but that's to be expected with bookshelf speakers so I don't consider that a flaw. You can perhaps deepen the bass a bit by moving them close to the walls/floor, but I found that muddies the sound for me. Not horribly so, but noticeably. If you're looking for chest-pulsing bass therefore, you'll want to add a sub-woofer. If you don't need that, the bass coverage is fine. Mid-range and high are good as well, without sounding tinny or hard or thin, including at high volume. Vocals are clear and what I"d call natural-sounding or smooth (I recognize those are vague). Vocals stayed true through several genres (rock, singer-songwriter, prog rock, etc). Instruments also were clear. You can pick out individual instruments on ensemble pieces for instance, classical piano comes out warm and clear and stands out within orchestral concertos. Full orchestras sound fine, maybe not as full.

For their price, these are an excellent set, better than certainly most bookshelf speakers I've owned, and I don't think worse than any I've owned. I'd call them significantly better than cheap speakers, and yeah, not as good as 3000 dollar speakers I've heard, but most of us don't have that kind of money for speakers. These are a sweet spot for sound and cost. Highly recommended

This is a pricey Bluetooth speaker, but a high quality one so you do get what you pay for here. It’s one of my two favorite ones (the other is the Jam Heavy Metal) and outside of the Jam is far better sound quality than the several others I own. If you’re looking for something that gives you “adequate” music and can handle a splash or two, this is overkill. But if you want rich sound and insurance against big rain (or worse, a dunk in a pool), it’s probably worth moving up to this one.

Pros:
IP67, highly water-resistant. I confess, I didn’t test this by submerging it as it says you can; I’m gonna just trust ‘em on this one

Rich, distortion-free sound. Despite its size, this can get quite loud (in a nice touch for those wishing to pump it up, the volume controls on the speaker, unlike most I own, work independently of your source device (i.e. you can max out your iphone volume and then in addition max out the speaker). Even at high volume the sound doesn’t distort. And the bass is powerful and thick (not sub-woofer but then, if you want that, get a sub-woofer. For a portable speaker, it’s perhaps the best bass I’ve heard). It’s also quite clear. In comparison to the Jam, I’d say the bass on this is better but the Jam just edges out in terms of clarity with treble/voice. The sound quality is also quite good as a speaker phone.

Connecting. Pairing via Bluetooth was pretty instantaneous with my iPhone and iPad. There’s also an audio-jack to plug in

Stereo potential. You can link it with another, though I don’t have a second so can’t speak to how it sounds

Size: it’s small enough to toss easily into a backpack if not a pocket. Has a heft to it in terms of a quality, durable build-feel, but not so as to strain you carrying it around at all.

Cons are all pretty minor
Buttons are a bit stiff (maybe this will change)

No charging cable with mine

Neutral: no connectivity with voice activation like Alexa
Charges in a few hours and last anywhere from 8-12 depending on volume, not the best but far from the worst

Personally, I hate tinny, thin-sounding speakers. If I’m going to listen to music, I don’t need it to be pristine, but I do want it to sound like my music, so I think this is a good value. The sound quality alone is worth it—it blows away cheaper Bluetooth portables— and combined with the high-level water resistance, it’s makes it an even easier recommendation

So far so good with the sturdily built, relatively compact, good sounding speaker

1) Packaging: packaging was minimal, no excessive space or paper or other such product and easy to open

2) The Jam came charged and I got a bit over six hours on the "shipped charged" battery. When I fully charge it and run it again I'll update. I assume the fully charged will up the hours

3) build quality is excellent. It certainly lives up to its "heavy" name. I wouldn't want to wander around the neighborhood with it, but who would do that? So I prefer the heft for the sense it gives of superior durability. This thing feels like it will stand up to lots of abuse, and it has a decent modernist look to it as well.

4) Pairing: it paired immediately with all my Apple devices, not a single issue with a MacBook Pro, an iPad2, and a 5th Generation iPod Touch. All recognized it, paired, and were playing music in seconds

5) Sound quality was quite good across the range. Very sharp and precise, especially in the treble range. I'm not sure I'd call the bass booming, but certainly solid and deep enough for me. Not at all tinny or weak sounding. And the volume cranks up pretty high without distorting.

Will update with a full battery, but for build quality and sound quality, Jam seems to have a winner with this one

OK, I’ll preface this by saying that while I have used Windows machines, I prefer Macs. So get that out of the way early. As for this particular laptop:
1) it felt a tad unresponsive to me, not horribly so, but noticeably so, at least in comparison to my 2-yr-old Macbook Pro. Certainly faster than my other, older laptop (5 yrs old), but still things seemed to lag a bit disappointingly
2) It’s nicely thin, you can see the dimensions and weight. It feels a bit heavy to me in terms of true portability, especially for having plastic parts
3) I wish it felt more sturdy. The top is strong, and the hinge feels nicely solid and durable. But the bottom and keyboard sections--the black plastic parts-- feel cheap. And I’m not a fan of the slightly rough texture on the trackpad. Keyboard is a nice full size. I prefer a very sensitive, speedy trackpad, so default settings were slow for me, but easy to change. I also find the glare from the black border a bit distracting at times.
4) Wi-fi and Bluetooth set up were easy and quick whether pairing devices or connecting to my network. No problems at all.
5) This isn't a review of Windows 8, so I'll leave that alone save to say I'm not a fan. If you are, this is it.
6) The touch screen is responsive and pretty accurate, though for the life of me I can't figure out who is looking for a touch screen on a laptop. Obviously, some people must like it, but I can't imagine using it hardly at all due to the horrible ergonomics of it. If you're looking for a touchscreen laptop, this seems more than sufficiently responsive and accurate.
7) screen is colorful and bright. Sound is solid--nothing to write home about, but not too tinny. It is a laptop after all. Certainly fine for streaming youtube videos and if you're not picky, movies.
8) Not sure I'm buying the battery life based on a few days of use, but I'll update as needed

It's always hard to compare cross platform. Given a choice between this brand new one and my two-year-old Mac, I wouldn't even consider switching. But then, this computer isn't really aimed at switchers I'd guess. If I can imagine just starting out neutral--probably impossible to do--I think I'd find it a mid-range product: a little noticeably slow in some respects, a tad heavy but not deal-breakingly so, some sense of durability in the aluminum and hinge but feeling a bit cheap in the other parts, decent screen and sound, very quick and easy plug-and-play-and-connect set-up, a "bonus" touchscreen that I probably wouldn't use at al.

This speaker has a surprisingly good sound for its portability. A few points:

1) it paired without any problem with all my devices--two iPod Touches, a Macbook Pro, an iPad Air (sorry, no Androids). Recognized and paired immediately with all and kept the connection throughout

2) As mentioned, I was very pleasantly surprised by the sound, which for this type of speaker was unexpectedly rich. As is always the case with a speaker this size, the bass will be the downside, but really, it wasn't bad in general and not at all bad for this type of product. Nor was the sound tinny, as can happen sometimes. Volume is decent--you aren't going to bring the walls down, but then, that's rarely the point of these. I've had three or four bluetooth speakers and this has so far been my favorite. And really by a pretty good margin.

3) it has a nice heft to it, feels solidly constructed and built, but looks pretty good and while it's larger than many bluetooth speakers, it's more vertical so the footprint isn't bad.

4) the battery is rechargeable, which is a nice touch, and for me ran nearly five hours the one time I ran it all the way to the end. If that is unusual when compared to future use I'll update

5) it's described as water resistant, but to be honest, I didn't decide to test that by pouring water on it or misting it. But it's good to know as I'll be using it a lot on the patio while I work or just sit out and enjoy the day. And I like the idea of tossing it in the trunk to use outdoors as well.

Really like it quite a bit and I'm hoping this early evaluation remains accurate throughout its life

It took me longer to unpack these than to get music via my iPod Touch streaming through them--the set-up, connecting, streaming process took under about two minutes. Worked fine as well with my laptop.

The sound quality is fine, especially for small speakers. I don't expect them to rattle my windows are pump the base. The lack of a strong bass is noticeable (as mentioned, not a surprise) but I wouldn't call them tinny at all. The sound was quite pleasing and handled high volume with no distortion.

They're small enough to pack or easily move around or outside. They do connect to each other, with detracts from their convenience a bit, and I personally wouldn't have minded a longer connecting cable so as to spread the sound a bit farther apart, but since they're really not made for room-filling sound--aimed more at desktop or otherwise small spaces, it's hard to call that a major complaint or oversight. A longer cable might have pleased me but had others complaining.

I prefer the Creative ZiiSound D3X to these--it's bit more convenient in that it's a single speaker set up and I thought its sound quality a little better, plus it has the ability to add in the subwoofer and other speakers (I have the subwoofer), but really, the difference isn't huge and the intent is somewhat different for most, so these speakers more than suit the bill for their size and purpose.

This is a decent recorder, but the recording quality is pretty tinny. I was surprised that the Lamyik I also tried had better quality despite looking less visually impressive. I'm not affiliated with them in any way, just giving my opinion based on trying both of them. I have two recording examples, I might post them later.

Superb, wide soundstage. Ridiculously good build quality that is better than a majority of headphones. High quality, braided 3.5mm detachable cable. Sound is very refined with great clarity, a bit warm with the entire spectrum seemingly emphasized. Excellent bass that doesn't muddy up the mids. Mids are not recessed and are also excellent. Treble also sounds great, but it can be a SLIGHTLY bit sibilant/harsh if you're treble-sensitive like I am. However this isn't a problem on most songs, and if you are really concerned about it you can bring it down by 2-3 dB with EQ (10kHz region). Most people aren't going to have this problem however, and I'm pretty sure it will tame over time (I have a pair of Grados that are notorious for their piercing highs, and after 5 years of use I have zero problems with the highs. Burn in must be real to some extent.). Overall, with their solid bass, great soundstage, and a frequency response that leaves no area recessed, movies, games, and music are superbly presented. Highly recommended

This retro boom box can be used with 4 D batteries or you can plug it in with the AC adapter. The battery option is good for using this radio at the beach but I noticed that it uses up the battery power fairly quickly. The plug in option is better though I wish it used USB as I have plenty of chargers for that. The sound quality is pretty good, not tinny, and the digital read out is cool. The reception is also good. There's nothing extraordinary about the sound quality (it's nowhere near Bose quality) but it's a nifty looking throwback to the old style radios. I think a hipster who wasn't around during the 70s would love this.

Updated review:

I've become somewhat dependent on the sight of this bright blue radio. Every morning I stumble, groggy-eyed, into my bathroom. Having this clear-sounding radio, blasting my favorite music, is a nice pick-me-up as I shower. But does the design offer me anything more than what I would expect from a typical shower radio?

PROS: It's cleverly designed to mimic the shape of a shampoo. It melds easily into the background. My initial fear was that I would accidentally grab it instead of the real thing, but so far that hasn't happened.

PROS: The sound quality is tinny but quite decent for a shower radio.

PROS: The radio offers a "store" function where you can bookmark your favorite radio stations and get to them fast by using a "recall" button. This is a feature common to most clock radios but I don't spend enough time in the bathroom to use it. I basically stick to one station while showering and can't see myself using the "store" function unless I'm taking a long bath. Still, nice to have that option.

PROS: Great battery life! I used my AA batteries for this and it has been running for months with no problem.

CONS: It's not that easy to see the buttons. They're located on the sides of the device but the positions are not intuitive. I always have to squint a little to see the print above the buttons because the buttons do not stick out.

CONS: "Light up" function. The time display is very clear and easy to read as-is. Since it's not a bedtime clock radio that benefits from having a glow-in-the-dark function, this feature feels extraneous to me. Perhaps it's best for someone who likes to take a bath with candles all around.

CONS: Not space saving. I used to have a shower radio that could be hooked over the showerhead. While the radio is not huge, I still had to move my shampoo and conditioner bottles to make room for it.

Overall it is a decent radio and I have been using it since I got it with no problems.

PROS: Easy to set up. All I had to do was plug the included Bluetooth wireless device into a USB on my Toshiba Windows 7 netbook. Soon I had the pleasure of listening to Youtube videos and my iTunes library through a thumping subwoofer and two speakers.

If you don't expect BOSE quality-like sound, a decent set of speakers for the price. At high levels the sound does get a little tinny, but still represents a major improvement over the sound of the typical speakers provided with a PC. The set is particularly useful if you're throwing a party in your small apartment and want to use your iTunes library as the source.

CONS:
The title of the product is misleading. It is not a true "wireless" device in the sense that the subwoofer and speaker are wired and have to be plugged into an outlet. However, I didn't mind this as many truly "wireless" devices often require batteries or have to be recharged at some point.

Do we need such a big fat subwoofer/speaker? It looks weird being sandwiched between two little ones. The trio takes up a lot of space and is awkward to store. I would rather have had two moderately-sized speakers with good bass. Also, the right speaker is permanently wired to the back of the subwoofer, while the left one is detachable. I would have preferred two detachable speakers.

The instructions are poorly laid out. Instead of having one or two manuals (i.e., one for a quick set-up, one with more detail), the manufacturer chose to scatter the instructions across several small booklets. One had a diagram showing how to connect it with an analog connection while another little booklet showed you how to connect wirelessly. Yet another listed the customary safety warnings and warranty. A waste of paper.

I have been looking for moderately priced bluetooth headphones for the gym, ones that stayed in place on the treadmill, and offered quality sound. These work so well. Secure fit--the design keeps the headphones in ear without having to constantly re-adjust. Fine sound --rich bass without mush, clear treble without that tinny sound. 3 equalizer modes that allow adjustment- and you can actually hear the difference and choose the one you most enjoy. The controls are easy to use once your fingers know where to press. The call quality through the headphones is very good. The battery life--have used for a few hours over 2-3 weeks and battery life is still "medium" (nice to be told  where the battery life stands each time you turn these on.) Okay, two side comments: they are a bit bulky due to extensive battery life and easy to use controls, but not to the point of hampering fit, and; the memory foam earpieces  did not work that well for me, and when trading them out to try the regular ones, they immediately ripped. No issue, though, cause i preferred the regular earpieces, and had a chance to order more free as well. All in all, a great purchase at a good price.

I bought two of these and they work great with my household Echo devices. However, the audio volume is best left below max so the tiny speaker doesn't sound shrill and 'tinny' or 'metallic'. Also, when audio is playing through the Echo Flex and I try calling it to switch to another song, sometimes it is not able to pick my voice over the audio. But that is a minor inconvenience. Great device to add to the existing Echo devices.

I bought these for use in my office, where I listen to music at a relatively low volume.  Speakers have a nice, clean sound and bass without boom.  I have not heard any 2.0 speakers that compare with a decent 2.1 outfit - a subwoofer just moves more air, period.  But for what these are, I get a quality sound that is not tinny - which tinniness is a common fault on the cheaper 2.0 sets.  However, if you rate yourself an audiophile, pass up all the 2.0 sets and go for a higher end 2.1.

That's a line from a Gin Blossoms song, that fit's these speakers. I wasn't looking for something to sound great, just something that didn't sound terrible, was small, and I didn't need another A/C power cord to run. This fits the bill and they will work when I just need a temporary or non-musical speaker.

Otherwise, the sound is tinny and mediocre. They will work for what I need them for, just don't expect great sound.

PS-Read all the other reviews about the annoying lights and didn't think it was a big deal. My new PC powers the USB ports even when the computer is off, so these lights are on 24/7 unless I unplug them from the computer. Annoying and useless.
Great setup and sound quality.  I have an inner ear piercing so I don't like earbuds that rely solely on staying in from pressure, it hurts. The ear hooks are great.

The name suggests it’s from Japan; not so, made in China.  IMO, the quality falls short of expectations despite being a very user friendly unit with good features.  HDMI allows for an easy connect to homeTV, not generally found on most DVD players.  Cable not included.  At this price the sound is too tinny.  Maybe earbuds improves it?  I would recommend it if you don’t mind average, e.g. Chevrolet quality but if you want Japanese or BMW fit and finish level look elsewhere.

I don't know what to think of these headphones. The sound out of the box is terrible, just abysmal. I've never heard a more unbalanced headphone anywhere. If you can't use an eq with these headphones, stop reading and look elsewhere.

If you can use an eq in your application, you might find these headphones surprising. Once the shrill high-end is toned down and the bass and mids bumped up, you will find the sound is pretty good for a ~$60/pair. The soundstage is small, but clear and the instrument separation surpasses what I was expecting. However, boost the bass too much and you will get distortion.

A couple of weeks before buying these I heard the quad-driver version and they were simply amazing. It was like I was sitting in my own living room listening to a full surround sound setup. I've never heard spacial definition or as big a soundstage in a headphone as I did with the quad-drivers, especially IEMs. The quad-drivers are on par with $600/pair HiFiMan planars. That's why I took a chance on this much cheaper bluetooth version of a single driver.

If you don't mind playing with the eq and don't want to buy cheap knock-offs from china (these are made in china, but by the company that designed them), take a chance on these. If you just want to plug and play, buy something else. I'm still on the fence on returning them myself.

I paired this with my Galaxy S4 and Nook HD+ Tablet. It was easy to pair and it works nicely switching from listening to Nook audio to answering a phone call. The sound is very good for audio books, music, and cell phone calls. No tinny or voices coming through a tube sound.

I very much like the small indiscreet size of the receiver. The buttons on it are easily found by touch and there is a tiny function light for various alerts like a call coming in or when pairing or charging, etc.

The ear buds have 3 different size soft and comfortable earpieces. They are so soft and flexible that I can use any of them without any discomfort.

I have not used it continuously long enough for it to drain the battery so I cannot comment on that.

I bought this as an emergency when my parents' computer speaker went out. Based on the reviews it seemed like it would do the job and it seemed simple which is all we needed.

The connections are very simple and its a good looking speaker. Ideal for placing in that little space beneath a monitor in front of the stand. The headphone jack and manual volume dial is also a nice touch.

So everything up to the point of unboxing and connecting was great. Then we turned on the sound. It is tinny, there was no bass or even midrange body, and there was tons of distortion even at a modest volume. The best way I could characterize it is an old AM clock radio with a single speaker from the 70s. There wasn't anyway I could push decent volume out of these speakers and I tried every combination of source and speaker volume I could figure. If I was trying to use this on a laptop I wouldn't even bother. Better off with a cheap pair of computer speakers from Walmart.

Giving it two stars really because it does work, it had nice features, and it plays sound for very little money. But if you want better sound than what comes out of a cheap radio, spend a little more and get a lot more out of it. I can't imagine this speaker being useful in any way.

I love it, I really do. It works wonderfully and is such a super adorable color! It does have a bit of a funky smell but then again anything plastic/rubber and so on does for a few days when new. It goes away within an hour or so of being out of the wrapping anyhow. The shipping was uber quick which I personally love! The only irks I have with this is 1. it doesn't have any side protection so if you pick it up sideways your tablet WILL slide out! 2. I also dislike the cords, there is no where to "hide" them with a tablet in it. You can barely close it. All in all it is a good product though. The keyboard works well and is quiet.  It is a great value just be careful picking it up like a book. Being the oddball I am, I "fixed" mine by making two stoppers by literally piercing the case and using two of my older, thicker flat back labret studs. To be fair it worked great and added my own cute/crazy flare to it!

I ordered these because I rearranged my desk setup at work and needed to extend the length of my existing earbuds without spending too much money.

This cable feels like it's made really well, but the difference in sound quality when using this cable vs. just my earbuds is too much for me to ignore. It sounded very tinny, muted, and there was almost no bass. I ended up returning them.

I heard these were like professional quality but i found them to be way less then that. I got a 20 dollar set of Behringer headphones that sound much better. These have a tinny sound to them, as well as when listening with them, i hear what sounds like an old 33 1/3 record scraping sound through them.  I do like the heavy duty cord but thats not worth a thing if the sound quality is jacked.

Perhaps not the fault of this particular earphone.
I bought these based on favorable reviews and low price. However, just like all previous earbuds I've tried, they sound tinny and
just wont stay in my ears. I guess it's just the shape of my ears. I'll just stick with my Grado SR80s.

This enclosure/cable worked perfectly and allowed me to recover a failed external drive.
My 6 month old external Seagate 1 TB USB drive failed. The drive inside the tinny Seagate case was a 2.5" Toshiba SATA HDD that seemed to be spinning OK so I assumed it was likely that the junky interface had failed and not the HDD itself.

Original review

So far I've tried
Skull Candy Titan - For me the best bass sound in this bunch. Tight punchy, accentuated but enjoyably so. Good for working out. But I value accurate bass above all. So I just use these for working out now.
Vsonic GR99 - very nice balanced sounding for $20ish dollars
Vsonic VC02 - Great sounding, but not a lot of bass. But what bass that was there was VERY good. My favorite phones in this list. But I kept losing the ear piece because of the removable wires. After the 2nd time I moved onto the VSD1
Vsonic VSD1 - nice sounding, if somewhat dry. It didn't make me get into my music, and I couldn't get them comfortable in my ears
Brainwaves S1 - These were my least favorite, boomy and not very comfortable, heavy thick wires. The only pair of the above I returned.

What they do well - assume anything not here is more than adequate

Presentation - I feel like I'm getting what the engineer was going for in the mix. More musical than any of the above without falling into a 'warm sound'. A nice mix of forgiving and accurate. Brightness right about where it should be.
Sound Stage - Airy, instruments well placed. Center image is not the strongest, but not lacking. Does a nice job of presenting the room acoustics/reverb in the mix.
Drums - Drums are rendered very well, better than any of the the above.
Cymbals - rendered very well, especially high hat. You can tell the cymbals are made of metal, and not just the tik-tik of the drum stick tip
Treble-sibilance - Close to perfect. Nice and bright without getting into hissy/tizzy. Vocal articulation is good.
Very easy to listen to for long periods of time. They are accurate without being piercing or harsh.
Sounded good right out of the box.

Misc sound notes - distorted electric guitar is just right. They respond to EQ very well, (which the Brainwavz did not do). I really notice when something comes into the mix even if it is soft. And louder things like guitar solos, really punch in the way you hear when mixing in the studio.

If I HAD to critique the sound (this is a review) there is a very-very, (did I mention very?) lack of something in the mids. Think chest/throat area of male vocals. But this is in the realm of sound signature, a matter of taste, not a deficiency and in no way lowers my enjoyment of these.

Build - wires are thin and flexible which is what I wanted. Very nice for wearing over the ear. Microphonics close to none whether worn up or down. No hearing foot steps or wire rubbing/bouncing on clothes. Light cord/cinch is great for running.
Shape - Bullet shaped what can I say, they are light and comfortable. I like the ring of rubber around them. It gives a little grip for inserting/removing them.
I LOVE that they have a red strain relief on the right side. No having to get my glasses to see some tiny R or L printed somewhere. Cord is nice and long, which is nice for using on a treadmill or elliptical trainer, or for wearing the cord under your shirt or down in a pocket.

As much as I liked the over all presentation and frequency response I feel I should point out these are not hella flat-accurate phones (like the VC02). If a true hi-fi sound, bright/accurate/revealing, is what you are after I'd look elsewhere (maybe the VC02) Don't get me wrong, since I used to be a sound engineer, and work on electric guitars, and have very accurate/bright/revealing/fatiguing speakers on my desk, I'm very picky about good accurate sound. But that makes these musical, easy to listen to for very long periods of time and poorly recorded and/or lower quality rips won't be hard to listen to.
