Unfortunately, they are just not good. The sound is very basic, tinny without any detectable bass.
Also, the voice that declares the status of the device is in what sounds like Chinese. I was unable to determine how to change the language, or if it's even possible.

You also better keep up with the charge cable that comes with these because I was only able to find one other cable in my whole house that would work to charge them.

As I said, I love the look. The digital charge indicator on the case has a really nice aesthetic.
I just can't recommend that you spend your money on them when much better earbuds can be found at this price point.

It seems to have everything you need, all kinds of options for connection which is nice. The bar looks good, you can tell by handling it that it's not the best quality but I was looking forward to hearing it, it has to be better than the tinny sound of my small tv. The instructions are terrible and only show the connections no other information. I hooked this up and nothing. I took the wires and plug out and tried again -nothing. I hate wasting my time. Maybe it's me but it's not working.

With the weather being crazy this year I figured I would get one of these for the house just in case we have our power knocked out by snow or ice.  Charging it is easy as it takes a USB c cable and if you don't have power it comes with a hand crank.  The radio is clear and the flashlight works great.  Be careful about clicking the SOS button as it does let out a piercing siren (I accidentally set it off in the morning while playing with it, my wife was not happy).  The only thing that disappointed me is it has a silicone cover for the USB port that is tethered to the device and it ripped right off when I tried to open it.  I was able to push it back together but that isn't ideal.  All in all, thought this will be a nice addition to my emergency kit, ill just have to watch it around water.

This is a pretty decent Android tablet that packs a lot of features for the price point. The overall build quality is excellent (again, giving the price point). It feels very substantial in hand – much more substantial than other under-$100 tablets I’ve tried. I especially like how all the ports and controls are clearly labeled (white on black) so there’s no guessing as to what’s what when it comes to external controls.

The screen resolution is very good for the price – more than adequate for enjoyable video watching, picture viewing, etc. The colors are rich and saturated. No complaints as to screen quality.

The touch control is also well-done. I didn’t have any problems with mis-clicks or having the screen not properly register a touch.

Setup is the same as any other Android tablet – pretty simple and straightforward. The user guide is sparse but pretty clear. It’s not necessary to refer to it if you’re familiar with Android, but if this is the first experience with that OS the manual provides enough info to get you up started.

Weak spots are audio and the cameras. The audio in particular is not well done. The sound is thin and tinny, and it gets worse at higher volumes. An external speaker is a must for this if you plan on getting enjoyable sound. Interestingly, the volume controls are not external buttons but are software-based. I like that since it cuts down on the button clutter on the edge of the tablet.

The camera is also not as well done as with other tablets at this price point, with less than ideal resolution and clarity, especially in lower light conditions. It’s workable but not at all impressive.

The tablet comes packaged in a pretty upscale fashion, with a nice box with foam cutouts. Add-ons are sparse – just a charger. Other tablets at this price point often include a richer set of accessories such as earbuds, a screen protector, case, etc. This is pretty bare bones – basically just the tablet.

While it’s not the best low-cost Android tablet I’ve tried, it certainly is competitive, especially with regard to the build quality and screen performance. Well worth considering if you’re looking for an inexpensive tablet that still provides a decent feature set.
[Sample provided for review]

This is a decent PC monitor that doesn’t excel in any area but, at the same time, doesn’t fall flat either (except for sound quality). It’s a good choice if you’re looking for an inexpensive, wide-screen monitor that comes in at under $100.

The build quality is what you’d expect at this price point: pretty basic and simple. The casing is all plastic, and rather cheap feeling plastic at that. It comes with a very basic stand that allows a limited amount of tilt adjustment, but no swivel or monitor rotation. There are no mounting holes on the back to facilitate a wall or stand mount. There are also no convenience features, such as a USB hub. It also lacks an HDMI port.

On the plus side, the power cord just plugs into the monitor without the need for a transformer or wall wart. The overall monitor profile is pretty slim, and it is very lightweight.

Setup is very simple. No tools are needed to attach the stand (just push and it clicks into place). It comes with a VGA cable, a 3.5mm audio cable and a power cable. Although it includes a DVI port, it does not come with the cable to use that. It also does not come with a user guide (other than a one-page quick setup sheet) or a driver disk. Both are available as downloads from the HP site. However, neither are really needed.

I hooked it up to my laptop via VGA to use as a secondary monitor. It auto installed under Win 7, so it should be able to do the same for 8 and 10. The recommended resolution is 1600x900 at 60Htz.

Right out of the box the settings were eye-searing bright, as is typical with manufacturer defaults since they want their monitors to stand out when on display in a store. Changing the settings is pretty easy – the menu button brings up the full list of options; you select the one you want; then adjust with the +/- keys. You can experiment at will since there’s also a choice to return to factory defaults should you get lost in the weeds with changes. The adjustment menu is pretty extensive for a monitor at this price point. You can adjust the usual brightness and contrast, and also color temp, image control, and even turn off the blue LED power indicator (yes!). Unfortunately, the control button labels are impossible to read (black on black) but there’s only a few buttons, so it's not tough to figure out.

The image quality is decent once it’s been properly adjusted. It won’t wow you, but it provides good performance on both images and text. I was happier with the text performance than I was with video (it has pretty limited black levels) but, for an everyday, inexpensive monitor, it’s more than acceptable.

The speakers are very, very basic. Tinny to the point of being useless. I’ve gotten better sound out of a $5 set of basic computer speakers.

I’m giving this 4 stars since, even at this price point, HP could have done a better job with the overall look/feel of the monitor, have included some additional convenience features such as a swivel, USB hub, and/or an HDMI port. Features that could have been dropped are the internal speakers, which are useless for anything other than to hear system beeps. Still, even as-is, it’s worth considering if you’re looking for a no-frills, no-fuss, inexpensive monitor.

Bottom line: Overall, this is an excellent laptop/tablet setup. The screen is simply gorgeous, the speed is excellent, and it easily morphs between a laptop and a tablet. Windows 8 can be a bit of a pain, as can some of the hardware design quirks, but overall, I’m finding it to be a solid performer. It's a good choice if you want a tablet but don't want to give up the functionality of a laptop.

Full review: It’s been a couple of years since I tried out a laptop/tablet “convertible” type system, and things have certainly improved for the better. This Asus is a fully functional system in both its tablet and laptop modes.

I was a little disappointed when I first opened the box since it was not packaged in a “high end” (ala Apple) manner. It was packed well in terms of protection, but it was pretty utilitarian. I also thought it was unusual that there was no setup or “welcome” sheet/poster packed with the hardware.

The utilitarian feel went away once I started using it. The overall fit and finish is excellent – very solid feeling. It is thinner than I expected – folded up it’s just a bit thicker than my older tablets. The tablet portion alone is sleek and solid. You do notice the weight when using just the tablet, but it’s not bad. My only quibble is that the tablet case is slippy in hand. The keyboard has non-slip feet on it that keep it well-planted, but when using just the tablet, it’s slidy. I’m shopping for a case or skin to help with the hand feel of the tablet.

Setup was straightforward, with Win 8 going through the usual setup process of a couple of minutes to get the basics taken care of, then an hour or so of having it fetch and install all the needed OS updates. I used Win 8 for a bit when it came out, but mostly work with Win 7 machines. It was a pleasant surprise to see how well Microsoft has buffed the rough edges off of Win 8. I can’t say that I love it (I'm more of an Android fan when it comes to touch screens) but it’s a very workable OS that is (mostly) easy to use. Granted, the very first thing I did was install Chrome since IE is a total pain, but overall, Win 8 is not bad. But, I want to keep this review focused on the hardware rather than Win 8.

The shining star of the tablet is the screen. It is absolutely gorgeous in terms of resolution, be it text (which was a treat for these old eyes since young programmers seem to think everyone can read 2 point type) or video. The viewing angle is excellent, the colors are rich and vibrant. Asus did an excellent job with the screen.

The touch sensitivity of the screen is also excellent. I don't use a stylus and am able to reliably hit everything I aim or swipe for. That’s saying a lot given my less than nimble fingers.

The keyboard is good but not great. The key feel is decent, as is the layout, but the keys and the frame feels cheap compared with the more solid feel of the tablet. The touch pad is decent, but there's not much need for it given the excellent touch screen. The docking between the tablet and the keyboard is very well made – easy to attach, pretty easy to detach, and it maintains a very secure grip. I had no problems switching between the virtual and the physical keyboard (which uses Bluetooth to connect with the tablet).

The tablet has no fan but does not heat up much. I can feel some warmth on the right side of the tablet back after it has been operating for a few hours, but it’s just warm, rather than hot. And I certainly don’t miss the fan noise. The internal drive is solid state, so there truly is zero operating sound. The claimed run time of about 8 hours is accurate.

The operating speed is snappy. I noticed zero lag time switching between apps/programs, and no significant slowdown when running multi-tasking programs. I attribute this to both a decent speed for the processor, plus the solid state drive.

The sound quality is just OK. It's pretty clear, but sounds tinny and lacks any measure of punch or bass. That's not surprising given how small the speakers have to be. The sound quality is adequate for basic audio, such as watching a YouTube video, but for anything else you'll probably want to use an external speaker. I paired it with an external Bluetooth speaker for streaming music, and even though the external speaker was not high end, the sound quality improvement was significant.

What I don’t care for is how USB devices are connected. It has a dongle which attaches to the tablet. It works, but it’s ungainly. I would have loved to have a conventional USB port built into the tablet (or keyboard) even at the expense of the needed extra thickness. On the plus side, the dongle worked fine with every USB device I tried it with (various external drives, printers, camera). In addition to the USB output it can read an SD card plus has an HDMI output port.

It’s a bit of a pain to open the tablet when it’s docked with the keyboard and folded up. The hinge tightness works against you when trying to get it open. Lastly, the charger has a wall wart on the end which can be problematic when trying to plug it into a loaded power strip.

While there are negatives, they are mostly of the irritating nature rather than the truly interfering nature. This is a solid device that provides excellent functionality as a tablet and provides good laptop functionality. The Win 8 OS allows you to use the full range of Windows application software plus an extensive number of apps. While it won’t fully replace a “real” laptop since it lacks items that I would want in a laptop (such as a built-in DVD drive and a better keyboard), it offers far more utility than just a tablet and does so at a good price point. The negatives drop it to 4.5 stars, but I’ll round up to 5 stars since the screen is truly outstanding.

I love how comfortable these ear buds are. I’ve always been pleased with Brainwavz earphone comfort, but these have raised the comfort bar even higher. I’m using it mainly with the tri-flange tips which I’ve tried with other headphones but didn't care that much for. With the S0's, however, the tri-flange fit very well, provide for good sound isolation, and stay put even when I’m on the treadmill. Very well done.

The sound quality is also quite pleasing. There’s ample bass without it being boomy or muddy. Just a nice, solid low-frequency response that sounds great. The mid-range is clear even at higher volumes. The only small shortfall is with the upper ranges, which are not as clear and sharp as they could be, and get somewhat shrill at high volumes. But at normal volumes it’s a nicely balanced sound, and considering the price, I would describe the sound quality as very good overall.

The build quality feels pretty solid. The cables are well-attached and have molded connectors at the ear buds to give it better durability. That’s important for me since, while this comes with a very nice carry case, I usually just wrap the cords around whatever device I’m using, which puts a lot of stress on the connectors. These feel more than solid enough to deal with that level of abuse. I have a few other Brainwavz earphones and have yet to have one fail on me.

This is well worth a spot on your short list if you’re shopping for a well-made, comfortable set of earbuds that deliver solid sound without breaking the bank. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]

Overall, this is a decent monitor provided you’re not looking for a high-res PC monitor. I’m using it mainly in its TV mode and have been very impressed with the picture quality. The built-in tuner works well (with one exception, as noted below) producing a rich image. It’s also very well suited as an extension for a small screen device, such as a tablet. I’m using it with my Kindle Fire (via HDMI), and it provides for an excellent viewing experience.

Although the native resolution is 1366x768 pixels, the screen size of 24 inches is small enough that the lack of full HD is not missed. What I did miss is the lack of adjustability of the stand. There’s no tilt or swivel – the stand just holds the screen in a fixed position. It really interferes with proper positioning if this is used as a PC monitor, and is also a problem when using it as a TV. While I don’t expect a lot of extras at this price point, the lack of any measure of adjustability is a big oversight.

If you’re familiar with Samsung TVs, the menu system and remote will be straightforward. If you’re not familiar with Samsung TVs, the menu system will take a bit of time to master with all the nested menus. There are a number of short cuts for various picture modes (such as “sports mode” and “movie”) which are simple to select. Once you get more familiar with the options you can delve deeper and make more specific tweaks.

The sound quality is not great – pretty tinny sounding and there’s little bass. An external speaker is highly recommended if you want to get any measure of impressive sound out of this.

The TV tuner is easy to program with channel favorites. I’m using it with an over-the-air antenna, and have been pleased with the number of channels and the signal strength. There is, however, an annoying long lag between pressing the channel up/down button and having the channel lock in.

The remote is typical Samsung – lots of buttons that are all the same size. Workable, but nothing special.

Considering the price point, I find this to be a 4-star product. It would be a 5-star one with the current feature set and limitations if the price were $50 or $60 less; it would be 3-stars should the price go past $225. A worthwhile choice for TV or small screen mirroring provided you can live with the limited adjustability.

This is a more upscale version of the “pop up” speakers that have been around for a while. It adds some useful features including an SD card slot to play mp3 files directly and more advanced controls, such as a toggle switch for track skip and a mute button.

When compressed it’s very compact, measuring roughly 2.5 inches in diameter. While it can be played in its compact mode, the sound quality is not all that great – very tinny with little bass.

The sound quality improves significantly when it’s popped open. That increases the height to about 3.25 inches. That doesn't seem like much, but it makes a huge difference in sound quality. The bass is far more pronounced and, while the mid and upper ranges are still somewhat muddy, it’s far more pleasant to listen to than when it is folded up.

Given the size, I’d rate the sound quality as very good when it is in its pop-up mode. This is not a room-filling speaker but it sounds a whole lot better than the internal speakers in a tablet.

It is a direct-connect only speaker – it does NOT have bluetooth. It comes with a 3.5mm cord that is permanently attached to the base of the speaker. The cable can be stowed in a grove on the base of the speaker. The attached cable is a plus and a minus: you’ll never forget to bring a cable along, but the cord is only about 5 inches long, which made it backward to use on some of my equipment. I like that the cord is attached, but it really needs to be a bit longer.

The build quality feels pretty solid. It’s all plastic, as expected, but it has a nice feel to it. The bellows section in the middle feels like it is build solid enough to last a while. Plus, the fact that you can close it up easily for transport gives me some measure of assurance that it will survive being tossed around a bit. For the price, I’d rate the build quality as very good.

There are less expensive pop-up speakers available, such as the Xboom. I have one of those as well, and when comparing the two side-by-side I thought the sound quality was bit better on the Sonpre. The Sonpre also has more features than the Xboom (the mute button in particular is a welcome addition) and has longer battery life. So, while it is a few bucks more, it does bring some additional features to the table.

Although the short cord drops my rating by a star, this is definitely one to consider if you’re looking for a decent sounding pop-up speaker.
[Sample provided for review]

This is a really nice looking mini speaker that is styled after a guitar amp. It allows you to connect any portable device that has a 3.5mm connection. I used it with a couple of different tablets (Fire, Nexus and iPad) with great results.

The build quality is impressive for the price. It’s mostly plastic, but feels very solid. The plastic has a leather-like pattern imprinted into it, again keeping with the overall amp theme. There are non-slip pads on the base that grip well on a tabletop.

I love how easy the controls are to use! No fumbling around with mini buttons – nice big old- style knobs you turn. The settings are marked 1 to 10 (sorry, no going to 11).

The sound quality is pretty good. It’s somewhat tinny and gets harsh at loud volume, but for normal listening it puts out a more than acceptable sound. The bass and treble controls make a noticeable impact on the sound – more so than I expected given the price.

There’s a cutout on the top to hold a phone. This is not an active dock – all devices are attached using a 3.5mm cord. The cutout is just that – a simple cutout that holds the phone.

It can be powered by 4 AA batteries (not included), a wall adapter (included) or a USB cable (included). I use it mainly with the wall adapter, but it’s nice that it can be made fully portable with standard batteries.

Misses are mostly minor. The battery door is held on with screws, so you need to have a screwdriver if you want to swap out the AA batteries. Also, the flap covering the “dock” port on the top is on the flimsy side.

This is something that you get more for the look rather than the sound quality (although the sound quality is pretty good as well). It’s one of the more novel looking small speakers I’ve seen, and well worth a 5 star rating.
[Sample provided for review]

Bottom line: while this won't shake the rafters, it puts out nicely balanced sound quality and offers a number of convenience features for ease of use. Outstanding bluetooth range. One of the better small speakers I've used.

Full review:
The problem with small speakers is that they tend to sound muddy or tinny. This speaker, in contrast, puts out some pretty decent sound. The treble and mid-range are well-defined, and the bass is surprisingly good given that it lacks a subwoofer. I found it better suited for movie dialog than music, but it did a capable job for both.

The overall design is quite nice. It's an oval shape that stands a bit over 7 inches tall. The design overall is attractive, with a metal grill and a high gloss black plastic shell. The base has a non-skid pad on it that keeps it pretty secure from sliding.

It comes with a charging cable, a short RCA cable, and a wall plug.

There is a front control panel that is very simple - vol up, vol down and mute. Key presses are clicky and solid, so there's no mistaking if the key press registered or not.

The back has an on-off switch, a micro USB input port for charging and a RCA port if you want to direct-connect the speaker to a PC or tablet (that has the appropriate output port). Best of all, it has a removable battery! That sounds like a minor issue, but I'm fed up with devices where I can't replace the battery -- when the battery fails I end up having to toss the device. This uses a cell phone type battery (BL-5C model Li-Ion batteries) that is readily available on Amazon. So, when the battery finally stops accepting a charge, it can be replaced for a few bucks.

I had no problems pairing this with a Nexus 7 and a Fire 8.9. Simple and straightforward - just press the bluetooth button on the front (which is also the mute button) and it paired.

The bluetooth range is outstanding. I started in the basement, and was able to get a solid connection at the far end of the room (about 30+ feet). I then held the speaker and walked up the stairs. It maintained the connection (with a few dropouts) on the floor above the basement. That was truly impressive!

Now, this is a small, single enclosure speaker, so don't expect to use it to fill a large room with sound. But compared with other single speaker solutions I've tried, this put out good sound quality, looks nice, has a user-serviceable battery, and an outstanding bluetooth range. The only quibble I can muster is that I wish the on/off button was on the front rather than the back. But that minor issue aside, this is a solid product. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]

I needed an inexpensive DVD player to use in the basement, but still wanted to have good picture quality. I gave this a shot (bought it used) and have been more than pleased with the results.

Setup was a snap if you have an HDMI port (basically just plug in the HDMI cable, plug in the power cord, and you're done!). The on-screen setup menus were decent. Lots of options to choose from including several picture quality choices. The manual sort of explains the options, but some "lets see what this does" is helpful as well, especially with the picture quality options.

The player feels a bit "tinny' but that's pretty much par for the course for low-ended DVD players. The remote is decent - the buttons could be bigger, but it's acceptable. No eject button on the remote, however, which was an unexpected omission.

The picture quality is excellent - rivals a much more expensive Oppo DVD. Much, much better than I was expecting at this price point.

I've tried to unlock this to play region 2 disks but have had no luck. Tried a couple of options listed on AV discussion boards, but so far nothing. If anyone has had success unlocking this to play something other than Region 1 discs, I would love to hear how you did it.

Overall, a great DVD player, and a good value even at the regular price. Highly recommend.

These are not the type of earbuds that an audiophile would even consider using, but, since I'm not an audiophile, I find them to be excellent. Very comfortable to wear - the added air cushion padding really helps keep them in place without any discomfort.

There's a dramatic difference in the sound quality based upon how it fits in your ear, so you'll want to experiment with the various sizes of pads included with the buds to find the ones that are right for you. For me, the small size pads resulted in zero bass and a very "tinny" sound. The mediums were better, and the large size were best - more than ample bass, and virtually total isolation from outside sounds.

No problems whatsoever with them falling out of my ear while working out.

Build quality is decent - on a par for the price charged. I tend to be a bit hard on earbuds, and usually wind up with frayed cords. This seems pretty sturdy, and I'm hoping it will put up with the type of abuse I tend to shell out.

My only complaints involve the length of the cord. Would really like it if it were about a foot longer. Plus, I like the Sony design where one cord is a bit longer than the other past the yoke. Helps you tell the R from the L easily, and makes it possible to loop the cord behind your neck. These have equal-length cords, but there is a slider that helps secure the cord in use, and keep it from tangling when its all mangled up in my pocket. The wear comfort and great sound more than make up for those shortcomings.

For the price, these are excellent earbuds.

I couldn't get the microphone to work (light was green) so I had to watch about 4 "how to get your microphone to work on windows 10" tutorials on Youtube until one of them actually worked.  I was finally able to test the microphone and could see the sound bar going up and down as I spoke louder and softer into it.  However, no matter  how many tutorials I watched, I could never hear myself through my headset to actually hear the sound quality of the microphone.  So, I don't know if I sound wonderful, super tinny or somewhere in between.  I'll keep working with it but at this point I have to give it a rest for a while.  The little pamphlet included with the microphone is absolutely useless and doesn't offer any troubleshooting.

The earbuds I received for review don't have external volume control.  I have to adjust the volume using my phone or whatever device I have these plugged into.  I had my husband call me and the call button on the earbud cord worked fine. These are fine for in the car and yakking on the phone but if you want to listen to music it would be best to get a much better set of earbuds.  These don't have any bass to speak of, and the sound is thin and tinny.  You get a couple more pairs of bud covers for a better fit.  No instructions come with these but it's not really necessary since they're easy to figure out.

What I like about this monitor:
1. Easy to set up - I used my previous monitor video cable and power cord and had it up and running in a few minutes.
2. Very clear resolution despite having an old video card.
3. It has an HDMI connection but I am using the regular VGA input and it still very clear.
4. A VGA and sound cord are included.
5. Very sleek, streamline black design which goes nicely with my other computer accessories.

What could be better:
1. The included instructions tell you nothing about how to make video and audio adjustments. I can't use a bright setting and it took a good while to figure out how to use the buttons underneath the screen. They are not intuitive at all.
2. Poor Audio - if you want good audio from this monitor that will not be possible. It is a thin monitor and the audio is very thin and tinny. I was hoping I could disconnect my external sound system to make more room on my desk but found out that I must keep it if I want to hear any decent sound from my computer.
3. While testing the volume on this monitor you must still figure out how to toggle using the various buttons underneath. There is no single volume button or toggle switch. And it will not get very loud.
4. If you don't bump the monitor or use the toggle switches the monitor stays fairly steady on it's stand. Otherwise it will rock and jiggle while using the buttons.
5. No HDMI cable is included.

The scant instructions did say to visit their website to download the latest drivers but as of yet this monitor is not listed in their driver drop down window. I don't think that matter much at this time as the monitor is very clear and sharp.
Overall: Good monitor for the price (as of this review it costs $138.24 Prime) which I feel is a fair price.

This thing is great! We already have a hard-wired security system in place including motion detectors. That said, if the power goes off for more than a couple of days or so our back-up battery is drained. So having these type of motion detectors that run off of 3 AAA batteries gives me a better feeling about security around the house. No, these do not automatically call the police when they are set off, but an ear-piercing shrill alarm is emitted that should cause most intruders (unless totally deaf), to change their minds and leave immediately.

These are very simple to install and set a 4 digit numeric password. I have ours set up facing the opposite direction of our other motion detector downstairs. The alarm will actually activate after 30 seconds upon detecting motion. I guess that's good or bad depending on how you look at it. 30 seconds is a long time to give someone access throughout your home and by the time the alarm goes off the intruder may have gone totally elsewhere in your home. But, it will give you a warning and let you get ready to do what might need to be done to protect yourself.

I had to write myself a note to remember to disable it when I go downstairs because I tend to forget it's there and it's scared the you-know-what out of me a couple of times. 30 seconds is more than enough time to disable it.

Installation is easy. It comes with all you need (except tools of course) and you can mount it at different angles as it has a swivel to let you adjust it wherever you think it needs to face. It works great in the dark so if you have pets that prowl around at night you might need to re-think your plans on how to use this alarm.

Overall, this is a pretty neat device for giving you a bit of piece of mind about your homestead and especially if you are on a budget. As I said earlier, I use these type of alarm systems as a supplement to our whole-house system that's hard wired to a monitoring company, but I l really like the extra monitoring in case of a prolonged power failure.

I bought several of these for our home and my mother's home. Super loud, and will stop or at least make it difficult for a door to be opened wide enough for an intruder to enter. I tested one out on my husband by placing it at the door he normally enters through. It stopped him, scared him and did just what I hoped it would do. He kind of got mad at me and hollered a few explicatives but it was worth it! We have one door that is on a raised threshold so I set the door stop alarm on a book and the door hits it squarely when opened just a little bitty bit. It's loud - ear piercing loud and that's good as it should scare the bejeebers out of a bad person. On doors that have windows through which the unwanted guest might peer through and see the doorstop, just by placing a light weight towel or papers over it disguises completely. They'll just think your a slob and leave newspapers on the floor.

My mom was thrilled with her doorstops. Anything to help parents stay safe is money well-spent.

Be aware of how all of your doors open since they won't do any good on doors that open to the outside. The 9 volt battery was a tad difficult to install but I'm not complaining. For my mom I had to write in big letters with a felt permanent marker ON and OFF so she could easily turn them off when not in use and not waste batteries or scare her by an accidental alarm. We'll be taking some of these with us on vacation. These are really great!

UPDATE: December 1, 2011 - I have bought several more of these because they are so practical and good at what they do. I've learned to pick them up by holding the sides of them lest I accidentally hit the metal plate on top and hear it's ear-breaking scream. I've taken at least one of these on overnight trips to put against the door in our hotel rooms. It makes me feel a lot safer knowing this thing will scream if someone tries to break in.

These earbuds come with 3 sizes of plastic pads but are set up with the medium sized one out of the box. The smallest pads worked best for me and fit reasonably well. The over the ear part did stay in place even as I powerwalked with a face mask.

The earbuds were easy to set up and pair with my Samsung phone. They came charged and it is not difficult to charge them with the USB cord. The volume is quite good and I did not find the sound tinny. While I don't have many pink items, these magenta earbuds are easy to spot in my black handbag, so the bright color is a plus. The earbuds are reasonable priced for their quality.
